summary: Hida and Coleman families, period modules and family L-functions, planned at target level in all eight layers (checkpoints 1–5 by cc-39fac3; completion pass by claude-LgrPjn, 2026-10-14). L0a (closed) owns the factorial ordinary projector: finite and profinite modules after Khare–Thorne and Hida, locally finite endomorphisms of complete modules and complexes after Pilloni §2 and BCGP §2.11, and the ordinary direct factor of a perfect complex; it cites IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.2 and DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P7 rather than replanning them. L0 plans Hida's ordinary Hecke algebras, control and Λ-adic forms; L1 the ordinary family symbol module, family periods and measures, the generic congruence module (owner for RT-AREA-langlands-1/27), Hida's family congruence modules and the branch L-functions of Emerton–Pollack–Weston. L2a is Buzzard's eigenvariety machine with the coherent eigenmodule sheaf and the spectral variety of a complex (Pilloni §13.1); L2 builds the eigencurves C^± from Stevens's overconvergent modular symbols (Bellaïche §3); L3 is Bellaïche's critical theory. L4 plans Hida's big Galois representation, family Selmer groups and complexes, Beilinson–Kato classes in Hida families, the family Coleman map and Ochiai's two-variable L-function and Euler-system bound, with a source-scoped Coleman-family regulator. L5 plans Hida theory over totally real fields (Skinner–Wiles's definite quaternionic towers, moved down from OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.1, and Λ-adic Hilbert forms with the facts Dasgupta–Kakde–Ventullo use). Every stage is planned (L0a closed); the remaining lists name refinements and the recorded gaps.

nodes.title: Katz's p-adic modular functions and the q-expansion principle
nodes.statement: For a p-adic ring A (A = lim A/pⁿA) and N = N₀pʳ with p ∤ N₀, V(N; A) is the ring of functions on isomorphism classes of triples (E, φ, i) over p-adic A-algebras — E an elliptic curve, φ : Ê ≅ Ĝ_m a trivialisation, i a level structure compatible with φ — compatible with base change; W(N; A) ⊂ V(N; A) is the subring of functions whose values at the trivialised Tate curves lie in A[ζ_{N₀}][[q^{1/N₀}]]. Evaluation at the Tate curve embeds V(N; A) in A((q)) with A-flat cokernel (the q-expansion principle), V(N; A) = V(N₀; A), and classical forms embed via ω = φ^*(dx/x).
hypotheses: p-adic rings in Hida's sense; the moduli of trivialised elliptic curves over p-adic rings is imported (ModularCurvesPartII R13.2 and Katz's theory of the Igusa tower).
proofSteps: Define V(N; A) functorially on trivialised triples; the Tate curve Tate(q) over ℤ_p((q))^ carries the canonical trivialisation.
q-expansion principle (1.8a–c): injectivity into A((q)), stability under change of A and A-flatness of the cokernel.
The compatibility condition (1.6) makes a level-N structure on a trivialised curve equivalent to a level-N₀ one, so V(N; A) = V(N₀; A).
Classical forms of weight k embed by evaluating on (E, ω = φ^*(dx/x)) (1.11).
acceptance: The q-expansion principle is stated with A-flat cokernel, not only injectivity.
The p-power part of the level disappears for p-adic modular functions (V(N; A) = V(N₀; A)).

nodes.title: p-adic modular forms are limits of classical forms (Katz)
nodes.statement: For p ≥ 5 or N₀ ≥ 3: W(N; ℤ_p) = W(N₀; ℤ_p) equals the p-adic closure M̄(N; ℤ_p) of ⊕_k M_k(Γ₁(N₀); ℤ_p) in ℤ_p[[q]], and modulo p, W(N₀; F_p) ≅ G(Γ₁(N₀); F_p)/(E_{p−1} − 1), where G is the graded algebra of mod-p modular forms of all weights; the isomorphism preserves q-expansions.
hypotheses: Hypothesis N₀ ≥ 3 or p ≥ 5 (Katz's Theorem 1.1).
proofSteps: Katz's Theorem 1.1 at full level Γ(N₀), from the Igusa tower being the étale Galois cover of the ordinary locus with group Γ = 1 + pℤ_p (Katz [16] §2, Theorems 2.1–2.2).
Descend to Γ₁(N₀) with the trace Tr(f) = N₀⁻¹ Σ_{u ∈ U₀} f|u, which is uniformly continuous and fixes E_{p−1} − 1 (Corollary 1.2).
acceptance: The mod-p statement uses the Hasse invariant E_{p−1} ≡ 1: it is the reason p-adic weights are congruent mod p − 1.

nodes.title: Hecke operators and the weight action on p-adic modular forms
nodes.statement: On M̄(N; 𝒪_K) (N divisible by p) the operators T(ℓ) and T(ℓ, ℓ) are defined by Hida's q-expansion formulas (1.13), agreeing with the classical operators on each M_k(Γ₁(N); 𝒪_K); they are p-adically contracting (|f|T(ℓ)|_p ≤ |f|_p), hence extend to the p-adic closure. The profinite group Z = ℤ_p^× × (ℤ/N₀)^× acts continuously by (f|z)(E, φ, i) = f(E, z_p⁻¹φ, z₀i), which on weight-k forms is z_p^k times the diamond action.
hypotheses: N divisible by p; the weight action is through Katz's modular interpretation.
proofSteps: Check (1.13) against the classical formulas on each weight, then extend by uniform continuity.
(1.12): on weight k, f|z = z_p^k f|γ with γ ∈ Γ₀(N) of lower-right entry ≡ z₀.
acceptance: T(p) = U_p for p | N; its q-expansion is a(n, f|U_p) = a(np, f).

nodes.title: Hida's universal Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: H_j(N; 𝒪_K) is the 𝒪_K-subalgebra of End(M_j(N; 𝒪_K)) generated by the T(ℓ), T(ℓ, ℓ), where M_j = ⊕_{k≤j} M_k; the restriction maps H_{j+1} → H_j are surjective and H(N; 𝒪_K) := lim_j H_j(N; 𝒪_K) is a compact ring acting faithfully and continuously on M̄(N; 𝒪_K). It is independent of the power of p in N: H(N₀pʳ; 𝒪) = H(N₀p; 𝒪). Cusp forms give h(N; 𝒪) likewise.
hypotheses: Each H_j is free of finite rank over 𝒪_K.
proofSteps: Finite freeness of H_j gives compactness; the projective limit of compact rings is compact.
Independence of the p-power: restriction H(N; 𝒪) → H(N₀p; 𝒪) is surjective and injective by Corollary 1.2.
acceptance: Over K (not 𝒪_K) the analogous limit does not act continuously; keep integral coefficients.

nodes.title: Hida's ordinary idempotent
nodes.statement: e := lim_n T(p)^{n!} ∈ H(N; 𝒪_K) (and in h(N; 𝒪_K)) exists, is idempotent, is compatible with every restriction H(N; 𝒪) → H_j(N; 𝒪), and on each finite level is the ordinary projector of T(p). For a module M over H(N; 𝒪) the ordinary part is M^ord = eM.
hypotheses: Instance of PadicFamilies L0a: each H_j is a finite 𝒪-algebra, complete for the p-adic topology.
proofSteps: Apply ordinary-idempotent-finite-algebra to t = T(p) in each H_j (finite over 𝒪, residue field finite).
Naturality (profinite-projector-natural) makes the e_j compatible under H_{j+1} → H_j; set e = lim e_j.
acceptance: Hida's own construction (Jordan decomposition modulo p and lifting) gives the same idempotent by uniqueness in L0a.
No averaging over a group order is used.

nodes.title: Duality between Hecke algebras and modular forms
nodes.statement: (Proposition 2.1) For A = K or 𝒪_K, H_j(N; A) ≅ Hom_A(M_j(N; A), A) and h_j ≅ Hom_A(S_j, A) through (h, f) = a(1, f|h). (Theorem 2.2) For p ≥ 5, H(N; ℤ_p) and M(N; T_p) = M̄(N; ℚ_p/ℤ_p) are mutually compact–discrete Pontryagin dual under the induced pairing, likewise h and S; (Corollary 2.3) the ordinary parts are dual.
hypotheses: p ≥ 5 in Theorem 2.2.
proofSteps: Finite level: (T(m), f) = a(m, f) gives nondegeneracy over K (Miller), then integrality over 𝒪_K.
Pass to Hom(−, T_p) with 0 → ℤ_p → ℚ_p → T_p → 0 and the limit over j.
(h h′, f) = (h, f|h′) makes the duality Hecke-equivariant, so e is self-dual.
acceptance: The duality is what makes H(N; ℤ_p) act continuously on M(N; T_p); the p-adic action alone is too weak.

nodes.title: The weight algebra Λ and arithmetic points
nodes.statement: Let Γ = 1 + pℤ_p with generator u = 1 + p and Λ_𝒪 = 𝒪[[Γ]] ≅ 𝒪[[X]] (γ = u ↦ 1 + X). The action of Γ ⊂ Z on M̄(N; 𝒪) commutes with the Hecke operators, making H(N; 𝒪) and H^ord(N; 𝒪) into Λ_𝒪-algebras. For k ∈ ℤ, P_k = (1 + X) − u^k ∈ Λ; the arithmetic specialisation at weight k is reduction modulo P_k. H^ord decomposes over the characters a mod p − 1 of μ_{p−1} ⊂ ℤ_p^× as ⊕_a H^ord(N, a; 𝒪).
hypotheses: p ≥ 5 so that ℤ_p^× = μ_{p−1} × Γ.
proofSteps: The Γ-action is by Hecke-equivariant automorphisms (the diamond action commutes with T(ℓ)), so ℤ_p[Γ] → H extends continuously to Λ = ℤ_p[[Γ]].
Idempotents of ℤ_p[μ_{p−1}] split H^ord by the character a.
acceptance: Use the power-series coordinate of ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 9 / PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1; do not rebuild Λ.

nodes.title: Jochnowitz's lemma
nodes.statement: For k ≥ 3 and p ≥ 5, T(p) annihilates the quotients M_{k+(p−1)}(Γ₁(N₀); F_p)/M_k(Γ₁(N₀); F_p) and S_{k+(p−1)}/S_k, where weight-k forms embed in weight k + p − 1 by multiplication by E_{p−1} ≡ 1.
hypotheses: k ≥ 3, p ≥ 5; the proof for Γ₀(N₀) works unchanged for Γ₁(N₀).
proofSteps: The filtration theory of mod-p forms: U_p lowers the filtration of a form of weight k + (p − 1) to at most weight k when k ≥ 3 (Jochnowitz, via the θ-operator and the Hasse invariant).
acceptance: Test: p = 5, k = 4: S₈(SL₂(ℤ); F₅) = 0 so the statement is empty; nontrivial checks start at k + 4 ≥ 12.

nodes.title: Ordinary mod-p forms live in bounded weight
nodes.statement: For p > 5 (Hida), there are q-expansion-preserving isomorphisms (M^ord(N; T_p)[p])^Γ ≅ ⊕_{a mod p−1} M^ord_{j(a)}(Γ₁(N₀); F_p) and similarly for cusp forms, with j(a) ∈ [3, p + 1] the representative of a.
hypotheses: p > 5 as printed (the corollary is used for p ≥ 5).
proofSteps: M(N; T_p)[p] = M̄(N; ℤ_p) ⊗ F_p = W(N₀; F_p) ≅ G(Γ₁(N₀); F_p)/(E_{p−1} − 1) (Corollary 1.2), which decomposes by weights mod p − 1.
Apply e: by Jochnowitz the ordinary part of each weight class stabilises at the smallest weight j(a) ≥ 3.
acceptance: The bound is what makes the ordinary Hecke algebra finite over Λ.

nodes.title: The ordinary Hecke algebra is finite over Λ
nodes.statement: For p ≥ 5, H^ord(N; 𝒪_K) and h^ord(N; 𝒪_K) are finite Λ_𝒪-modules, and H^ord(N; 𝒪_K) = H^ord(N; ℤ_p) ⊗_{ℤ_p} 𝒪_K.
proofSteps: By duality, finiteness over Λ is equivalent to cofiniteness of the Pontryagin dual M^ord(N; T_p) over Λ.
The Γ-invariants of its p-torsion are finite (Theorem 4.2), so by topological Nakayama over Λ (local with residue field F_p) the dual is cofinitely generated.
acceptance: Compactness plus finiteness of the Γ-invariants of the p-torsion, not a bound on individual weights, gives finiteness.

nodes.title: Hida's control theorem
nodes.statement: For p ≥ 5 and p | N: H^ord(N; 𝒪_K) and h^ord(N; 𝒪_K) are free of finite rank over Λ_𝒪, with rank_Λ H^ord(N, a) = rank_{ℤ_p} M_k^ord(Φ; ℤ_p) for every k ≥ 3 with k ≡ a mod p − 1 (and similarly for cusp forms with k ≥ 2). Restriction induces isomorphisms H^ord(N, a)/P_k H^ord(N, a) ≅ H_k^ord(Γ₁(N₀p), ω^{a−k}; 𝒪_K) for k ≥ j(a), and h^ord(N, a)/P_k ≅ h_k^ord(Γ₁(N₀p), ω^{a−k}; 𝒪_K) for k ≥ 2.
hypotheses: p ≥ 5 and p | N; ω the Teichmüller character; the finite-level algebras are those of weight k, level N₀p and nebentypus ω^{a−k}.
proofSteps: Freeness: the dual M^ord(N; T_p) is Λ-cofree because its P_k-torsion has constant ℤ_p-corank equal to the rank of classical ordinary forms of weight k (Theorem 4.2 and the classical dimension count), so the finite Λ-module H^ord has no P_k-torsion for infinitely many k and is free (Λ is a two-dimensional regular local ring) (§5).
Control: (H^ord/P_k)^∨ = M^ord[P_k] is the space of ordinary forms of weight k, level N₀p and character ω^{a−k}, for k in the stated range; dualise.
acceptance: The weight range differs for modular forms (k ≥ j(a)) and cusp forms (k ≥ 2).
Finite flatness is over Λ; do not assume the local components are Gorenstein.

nodes.title: The ordinary Λ-adic Eisenstein family
nodes.statement: For an even Dirichlet character ψ (conductor prime to p, allowing trivial), the Λ-adic q-expansion 𝓔_ψ = (constant term) + Σ_{n≥1} (Σ_{d|n, p∤d} ψ(d)⟨d⟩ d⁻¹) qⁿ ∈ Λ[[q]] ⊗ Frac Λ, built from DirichletPadicLFunctions L4's measure-valued q-expansion, specialises at each arithmetic point P_k (k ≥ 2, suitable parity) to the ordinary p-stabilised Eisenstein series E_k^{(p)}(ψω^{−k}) (so E_k^{(p)}(ψ) when k ≡ 0 mod p − 1), since ⟨d⟩ mod P_k = ⟨d⟩^k; it is an eigenfamily for all T(ℓ) with U_p-eigenvalue 1. Its constant term is the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudomeasure (a pole at the trivial character when ψ = 1).
hypotheses: RS-08: the Eisenstein family is imported from DirichletPadicLFunctions L4's measure; this node only identifies it as an ordinary Λ-adic form.
proofSteps: The positive coefficients are the Λ-valued measures of DPLF L4; their specialisations are the divisor sums of E_k^{(p)} (positive-eisenstein-series-modular-comparison).
U_p acts by 1 on the p-stabilised series (divisors prime to p), so the family is fixed by e.
acceptance: The constant term is a pseudomeasure, not an element of Λ, when ψ = 1.

nodes.title: Specialisation to classical ordinary forms
nodes.statement: Let F ∈ S^ord(N, a; Λ) be a normalised Λ-adic eigenform (a Λ-algebra homomorphism h^ord(N, a) → I, I finite over Λ). For every arithmetic point P of I above P_k (k ≥ 2), F mod P is the q-expansion of a classical normalised ordinary eigenform of weight k, level N₀p (or N₀pʳ for characters of conductor pʳ), nebentypus ω^{a−k} (times the finite character); if it is old at p it is the ordinary p-stabilisation f_α(z) = f(z) − β f(pz) of a newform f of level prime to p with α the unit root of X² − a_p(f)X + p^{k−1}χ(p), and the ordinary p-stabilisation is unique.
hypotheses: k ≥ 2; ordinary forms of level prime to p enter through their unique unit-root stabilisation.
proofSteps: Control (Corollary 3.2) identifies h^ord/P_k with the classical ordinary Hecke algebra, so the specialised eigensystem is classical.

p-stabilisation (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L2): exactly one root of X² − a_pX + p^{k−1}χ(p) is a unit when a_p is, giving a unique ordinary stabilisation; multiplicity is recorded (the other stabilisation is not ordinary).
acceptance: Record nebentypus, p-stabilisation and multiplicity at each arithmetic point; do not identify P with a unique vector.

nodes.title: Critical-slope, critical and θ-critical refinements
nodes.statement: Let f be a newform (cuspidal or Eisenstein) of weight k + 2 and level Γ₁(N), p ∤ N, with Hecke polynomial X² − a_pX + ε(p)p^{k+1} having distinct roots α, β. The refinement f_β (the p-stabilisation with U_p-eigenvalue β) has critical slope if v_p(β) = k + 1; it is critical if the equivalent conditions of criticality-equivalences hold (non-classical overconvergent generalised eigenforms, equivalently the eigencurve is not étale over weight space at f_β, equivalently ρ_f|_{D_p} is split with β on the weight-filtration line); it is θ-critical if f_β lies in the image of θ^{k+1} : M†_{−k} → M†_{k+2}. Critical implies critical slope; for cuspidal f, critical ⇔ θ-critical.
hypotheses: α ≠ β; ρ_f is Bellaïche's preferred representation (crystalline at p, indecomposable).
proofSteps: Record the three notions separately: slope (valuation), criticality (local Galois/eigencurve geometry), θ-criticality (image of θ^{k+1} on overconvergent forms).
acceptance: RS-08: keep 'slope k + 1', 'θ-critical' and 'critical refinement' distinct; ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L3 imports this distinction.

nodes.title: Equivalent forms of criticality
nodes.statement: For a refined form f_β the following are equivalent: (i) M_{k+2}(Γ)(f_β) ⊊ M†_{k+2}(Γ)(f_β) (non-classical generalised eigenforms); (i′) dim M†_{k+2}(Γ)(f_β) ≥ 2; (ii) v_p(β) > 0 and the eigencurve C is not étale over weight space at x = f_β; (iii) v_p(β) > 0 and ρ_f|_{D_p} is a direct sum of two characters; (iv) the β-line of D_cris(ρ_f|_{D_p}) equals the weight-filtration line. Then v_p(β) = k + 1. For cuspidal f these are equivalent to (v) θ-criticality; for Eisenstein f, (v) always holds.
hypotheses: The equivalences (iii) ⇔ (v) (Breuil–Emerton), (i) ⇔ (iii) for Eisenstein series (Bellaïche–Chenevier) and Coleman's limit control theorem are cited by Bellaïche and not decomposed here.
proofSteps: (i) ⇔ (i′) ⇔ (ii): Bellaïche Lemma 2.9 (étaleness of the weight map at x versus the dimension of the generalised eigenspace of overconvergent forms).
(iii) ⇔ (iv): weak admissibility of D_cris.
(v): Coleman's limit control theorem makes coker θ^{k+1} on the generalised eigenspace equal to S_{k+2}(Γ)(x).
acceptance: Keep the cited inputs visible in hypotheses; they are not proved here.

nodes.title: Which newforms have critical-slope refinements
nodes.statement: A newform f has a refinement of critical slope iff (a) f is cuspidal, not CM and ordinary at p; (b) f is cuspidal CM by K with p split in K; or (c) f is Eisenstein; the critical-slope refinement is then unique. In case (b) it is critical (hence θ-critical); in case (c) it is θ-critical, and non-critical when p is regular; in case (a) non-criticality is conjectural.
proofSteps: v_p(β) = k + 1 forces v_p(α) = 0, i.e. f ordinary; for CM forms this means p split.
CM: ρ_f|_{D_p} is a sum of two characters, so (iii) holds.
acceptance: Test on X₀(32) (CM, p ≡ 1 mod 4) and on an Eisenstein series of level Γ₀(11), p = 3.

nodes.title: Decent refinements
nodes.statement: f_β is decent if (i) f is Eisenstein, or (ii) f_β is non-critical, or (iii) f is cuspidal and H¹_g(G_ℚ, ad ρ_f) = 0. Sufficient conditions for (iii) (Proposition 2.15): ρ̄_f|_{G_L} absolutely irreducible for the quadratic L ⊂ ℚ(ζ_{p³}); or ρ̄_f reducible with characters distinct on G_{ℚ(ζ_{p^∞})}; or f non-CM and cuspidal/special at all primes dividing N; or f CM.
hypotheses: H¹_g is the Bloch–Kato geometric Selmer group; its vanishing is proved by Kisin/Weston/Rubin in the listed cases (cited).
proofSteps: Record the three alternatives; the listed criteria are cited results.
acceptance: Every CM form is decent; cuspidal non-CM forms are conjecturally doubly decent.

nodes.title: The eigencurve is smooth at decent points
nodes.statement: If f is decent (and v_p(β) ≠ 0 when f is Eisenstein), the eigencurve C (and its cuspidal part C₀) is smooth at the point x of f_β; its weight map has some ramification index e ≥ 1 at x, with e > 1 iff f_β is critical.
hypotheses: Chenevier's argument through the tangent space of the Galois deformation functor (cited).
proofSteps: Bound the tangent space of C at x by the refined deformation space of ρ_f, of dimension ≤ 1 + dim H¹_g(ad ρ_f) = 1 under decency; C is equidimensional of dimension 1, so smooth.
acceptance: Smoothness is what makes the local Hecke algebra a DVR (family-symbols-free-rank-one).

nodes.title: The θ exact sequence
nodes.statement: There is an exact sequence of ℚ_p[S₀(p)]-modules 0 → D_{−2−k}(k + 1) →^{Θ_k} D_k →^{ρ_k} V_k → 0, where ρ_k(μ) = ∫(Y − zX)^k dμ(z) and Θ_k is dual to the k-th derivative (the (k + 1) is a determinant twist); it induces an exact, Hecke- and ι-equivariant sequence 0 → Symb_Γ(D_{−2−k})(k + 1) →^{Θ*_k} Symb_Γ(D_k) →^{ρ*_k} Symb_Γ(V_k).
hypotheses: D_k are the weight-k distribution modules of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L2.
proofSteps: Dualise 0 → P_k → A → A →^{d^{k+1}} … : the kernel of the (k + 1)-st derivative on locally analytic functions is the polynomials of degree ≤ k.
Apply Hom_Γ(Δ₀, −), which is left exact.
acceptance: The sequence of symbols is exact only on the left three terms; surjectivity of ρ*_k is part of Stevens' control theorem.

nodes.title: Family modular symbols are free of rank one at decent points
nodes.statement: Let T±_{W,ν} be the Hecke algebra acting on Symb±_Γ(R ⊗̂ D)_{≤ν} over an affinoid W = Sp R of weight space and C±_{W,ν} the corresponding piece of the eigencurve. If x is a smooth point, the localisation Symb±_Γ(R ⊗̂ D)_(x) is free of finite rank over (T±_{W,ν})_(x) (a DVR), and the specialisation (T±_{W,ν})_(x) ⊗ ℚ̄_p → (T±_{w,ν})_(x) is an isomorphism; if x is a decent refined newform, the rank is one.
hypotheses: DVR lemma: a module over a DVR R that is finite over a finite free R-algebra T which is itself a DVR, and free over R, is free over T (Lemma 4.1; false for T merely local, Remark 4.2).
proofSteps: Lemma 4.1 at the smooth point x (C reduced, so the local ring is a DVR).
Rank one: near x all classical points are étale newform points with one-dimensional eigenspaces (Prop 3.18, Lemma 2.9).
acceptance: Test the DVR lemma's failure for T local but not a DVR (Remark 4.2).

nodes.title: Bellaïche's theorem on critical eigensymbols
nodes.statement: For a decent refinement f_β (v_p(β) > 0 if f is Eisenstein), Symb±_Γ(D_k)[f_β] is one-dimensional for both signs, and the following are equivalent: (i) f_β is critical; (ii) the generalised eigenspaces Symb±_Γ(D_k)(f_β) have dimension > 1; (iii) ρ*_k(Symb±_Γ(D_k)[f_β]) = 0 for both signs. For cuspidal f, (TS±) for one sign implies it for the other; for Eisenstein f, (TS^{−ε(f_β)}) always holds.
hypotheses: Decency; this extends Stevens (non-critical slope) and Pollack–Stevens (non-θ-critical) to the θ-critical case.
proofSteps: The eigenspace is the socle t^{e−1}Symb±(f_β) of the free rank-one ℚ̄_p[t]/(t^e)-module: dimension 1.
If e > 1 the eigenline is t^{e−1}·(generator) and ρ*_k kills it (Corollary 4.8); if e = 1 its image is the classical eigenline for cuspidal f.
acceptance: Distinguish critical slope from failure of ρ*_k to be an isomorphism: the latter is criticality.

nodes.title: The critical p-adic L-function
nodes.statement: For decent f_β and a generator Φ±_{f_β} of Symb±_Γ(D_k)[f_β], L±(f_β, σ) := Φ±_{f_β}({∞} − {0})(σ) for continuous σ : ℤ_p^× → ℂ_p^× (extended by 0 on pℤ_p); L(f_β, σ) = L⁺ + L⁻. It is analytic in σ (a power series in s on |s − 1| < 1 for each tame character), of order ≤ v_p(β), defined up to a nonzero scalar for each sign, and equals the Mazur–Tate–Teitelbaum / Pollack–Stevens p-adic L-function when f_β is not θ-critical.
hypotheses: Decency, so that the eigenline is one-dimensional.
proofSteps: Evaluate at {∞} − {0}, restrict to ℤ_p^×, take the Mellin transform (Amice).
Order ≤ v_p(β): the distribution Φ±({∞} − {0}) is v_p(β)-admissible (Višik).
acceptance: Interpolation determines L± only when v_p(β) < k + 1; at critical slope it does not.

nodes.title: Vanishing at classical characters in the θ-critical case
nodes.statement: If f_β is θ-critical then L±(f_β, ϕt^j) = 0 for every finite-order ϕ and 0 ≤ j ≤ k, except when f is Eisenstein, f_β non-critical, ± = ε(f_β), ϕ trivial and j = k. Equivalently each s ↦ L±(f_β, ψχ_s) is divisible by log^{[k]}(s) = ∏_{i=0}^{k} log_p(γ^{−i}s) (by log^{[k]}(s)/(s − γ^k) in the exceptional case).
hypotheses: θ-criticality: the eigensymbol lies in the image of Θ*_k.
proofSteps: Φ± ∈ image of Θ*_k ⇒ the distribution Φ±({∞} − {0}) kills polynomials of degree ≤ k twisted by finite-order characters (Θ_k is dual to d^{k+1}), so the classical values vanish.

proofSteps: An analytic function of order k + 1 on the open unit ball with prescribed behaviour at the zeros of log^{[k]} has infinitely many zeros (Weierstrass/Lazard theory of zeros).

proofSteps: Choose a generator Φ of Symb±_Γ(R ⊗̂ D)_(x) over the local Hecke algebra; evaluate at {∞} − {0} and Mellin-transform in families (Prop 4.11).
Specialisation at y gives a generator of the eigenline of y (Lemmas 4.12–4.13, Prop 4.14).

nodes.title: Factorial iterates of a self-map of a finite set stabilise
nodes.statement: Let X be a finite set with m = |X| elements and f : X → X any map. For every n ≥ m, f^[n!] = f^[m!]; the map e = f^[m!] is idempotent (e ∘ e = e); its image is the eventual image ⋂_k f^[k](X); and f restricts to a bijection of that image, whose inverse there is f^[m! − 1]. Equivalently, in the finite monoid of self-maps of X, the powers f^{n!} are eventually constant, with value the unique idempotent among the powers of f.
hypotheses: X finite (no algebraic structure is used); m = |X| ≥ 0, with 0! = 1.
proofSteps: For x ∈ X the orbit x, f(x), f²(x), … has at most m distinct points, so (pigeonhole) there are i(x) < j(x) ≤ m with f^{i(x)}(x) = f^{j(x)}(x); put ℓ(x) = j(x) − i(x) ≤ m. Then f^{a}(x) = f^{b}(x) whenever a, b ≥ i(x) and a ≡ b mod ℓ(x).
For n ≥ m: n! ≥ n ≥ m ≥ i(x) and ℓ(x) | n! (as ℓ(x) ≤ m ≤ n), so f^{n!}(x) = f^{m!}(x) and f^{2·m!}(x) = f^{m!}(x); hence f^[n!] = f^[m!] and e ∘ e = e.

Image: e(X) ⊆ f^[k](X) for k ≤ m!, and for k ≥ m! the chain f^[k](X) is constant from k = m on (a decreasing chain of subsets of an m-element set stabilises after at most m steps), so e(X) = ⋂_k f^[k](X).
On e(X), f ∘ f^[m!−1] = f^[m!−1] ∘ f = e = id, so f is a bijection of e(X) with inverse f^[m!−1] (m! ≥ 1).
acceptance: The threshold is explicit: n ≥ |X|; no bound uniform in a family of sets is claimed.
No group-order averaging and no division by m! is used: the argument works in every characteristic.
Test: on ZMod 6, x ↦ 2x has f^[6!] = (x ↦ 4x), which is idempotent (16 ≡ 4 mod 6).

sources.match: The eventual constancy of T^{n!}; here proved for any self-map of a finite set, as the stage requires (finite-set argument).

nodes.title: Hida's ordinary projector on a finite module
nodes.statement: Let R be a ring, M an R-module whose underlying set is finite, m = |M|, and U ∈ End_R(M). The ordinary projector is e_U := U^{m!} ∈ End_R(M). It satisfies e_U = U^{n!} for every n ≥ m (so e_U = lim_n U^{n!} in the discrete topology), e_U² = e_U and U e_U = e_U U. The ordinary part is M_ord := e_U M and the non-ordinary part is M_nord := ker e_U = (1 − e_U)M.
hypotheses: R any ring (not necessarily commutative); M finite as a set, e.g. a finite module over R/I with R/I finite.
U is R-linear; the construction uses only the monoid structure of End_R(M).
proofSteps: Apply factorial-iterate-stabilises to the underlying map of U: U^{n!} = U^{m!} for n ≥ m and U^{m!} is idempotent.
e_U is a power of U, hence R-linear and commuting with U.
acceptance: Changing m to any upper bound N ≥ |M| gives the same endomorphism (U^{N!} = U^{m!}).
A supplied idempotent is not a substitute: e_U is defined from U alone.
Units give e_U = 1 and nilpotents give e_U = 0.

sources.match: Khare–Thorne's projector e = lim T^{n!}; for a finite module the limit is attained at n = |M|.

nodes.title: The ordinary projector is the Fitting projection
nodes.statement: For M finite as a set and U ∈ End_R(M): range e_U = ⨅_n range(Uⁿ) and ker e_U = ⨆_n ker(Uⁿ). Hence e_U is the projection of M onto ⨅_n range(Uⁿ) along ⨆_n ker(Uⁿ) in Mathlib's Fitting decomposition LinearMap.isCompl_iSup_ker_pow_iInf_range_pow, and both chains are constant from n = |M| on.
hypotheses: M is Artinian and Noetherian (isArtinian_of_finite; Noetherian by the finite-set instance).
proofSteps: range e_U = range U^{m!} ⊆ range Uⁿ for n ≤ m!, and range Uⁿ is constant for n ≥ m (factorial-iterate-stabilises, image clause), so range e_U = ⨅ range Uⁿ.
ker e_U ⊇ ker Uⁿ for n ≤ m!; if Uⁿx = 0 then e_U x = U^{N!}x = 0 for N ≥ max(m, n); so ker e_U = ⨆ ker Uⁿ.
An idempotent is the projection onto its range along its kernel (LinearMap.isProj_iff_isIdempotentElem); compare with LinearMap.linearProjOfIsCompl for the Fitting complement pair.
acceptance: State the comparison as an equation of linear maps with the Mathlib projection, not only as equal submodules.

sources.match: M_ord = eM and M_nord = (1 − e)M; the Fitting identification is the comparison with Mathlib's decomposition.

nodes.title: U is invertible on the ordinary part and nilpotent on the rest
nodes.statement: For M finite as a set and U ∈ End_R(M): U maps M_ord and M_nord into themselves; U restricts to an R-linear automorphism of M_ord, whose inverse is the restriction of U^{m! − 1} (m = |M|); and U^m vanishes on M_nord.
hypotheses: m = |M| ≥ 1 (M contains 0).
proofSteps: U commutes with e_U, so it preserves range e_U and ker e_U.
On M_ord, U^{m!−1} ∘ U = U ∘ U^{m!−1} = e_U = id, giving the inverse.
ker Uⁿ is an increasing chain of subgroups of an m-element group; each strict step at least doubles the size, so it is constant from n = ⌊log₂ m⌋ ≤ m on, and M_nord = ⨆ ker Uⁿ = ker U^m.
acceptance: The exponent m on M_nord is uniform for this finite module; no uniform exponent exists for the profinite limit (profinite-ordinary-decomposition).

sources.match: Invertibility of T on the ordinary part (Khare–Thorne's route is via the lifted factorisation P = AB).

nodes.title: Uniqueness of the ordinary decomposition
nodes.statement: For M finite as a set and U ∈ End_R(M), M = M_ord ⊕ M_nord with both summands U-stable, U bijective on M_ord and nilpotent on M_nord. Conversely, if M = A ⊕ B as R-modules with U mapping A bijectively onto A and every element of B killed by some power of U, then A = M_ord and B = M_nord; U-stability of B need not be assumed.
hypotheses: M finite as a set; the summands are R-submodules.
proofSteps: Existence: e_U is idempotent, so M = range e_U ⊕ ker e_U; apply ordinary-part-bijective.
Uniqueness: U(A) = A gives A = Uⁿ(A) ⊆ range Uⁿ for all n, so A ⊆ ⨅ range Uⁿ = M_ord; every b ∈ B lies in some ker Uⁿ, so B ⊆ ⨆ ker Uⁿ = M_nord (finite-fitting-comparison).
Since M = A ⊕ B = M_ord ⊕ M_nord are finite, |A|·|B| = |M_ord|·|M_nord| with |A| ≤ |M_ord| and |B| ≤ |M_nord|, so both inclusions are equalities.
acceptance: The comparison is by inclusion and counting; no stability hypothesis on B is used, and U(A) = A (not merely U(A) ⊆ A with U injective on A) is what the statement asks.
Test: U = diag(1, 0) on (ZMod 2)²: the complement B = span(e₁ + e₂) of A = span(e₁) is excluded because Uⁿ(e₁ + e₂) = e₁ ≠ 0.

sources.match: Khare–Thorne Lemma 2.10(1), statement.
The two defining properties; for finite modules topological nilpotence is nilpotence.

nodes.title: Naturality of the ordinary projector
nodes.statement: Let M, N be R-modules that are finite as sets, U₁ ∈ End_R(M), U₂ ∈ End_R(N), and f : M → N R-linear with f U₁ = U₂ f. Then f e_{U₁} = e_{U₂} f; in particular f(M_ord) ⊆ N_ord and f(M_nord) ⊆ N_nord.
hypotheses: Khare–Thorne print T₂ ∈ End_R(M); the endomorphism of N is meant (sourceIssues).
proofSteps: Take n ≥ max(|M|, |N|): e_{U₁} = U₁^{n!} and e_{U₂} = U₂^{n!}, and f U₁^{n!} = U₂^{n!} f by induction.
acceptance: The same n must serve both modules; this is why the threshold n ≥ |M| (not a fixed exponent) is recorded.

sources.match: Khare–Thorne Lemma 2.10(2).
Hida uses this compatibility along the level tower.

nodes.title: Exactness of the ordinary part on finite modules
nodes.statement: Let M' → M → M'' (maps f, g) be exact at M, with M', M, M'' R-modules finite as sets and endomorphisms U', U, U'' such that f U' = U f and g U = U'' g. Then ker g ∩ M_ord = f(M'_ord), and if g is surjective then g(M_ord) = M''_ord. Hence M ↦ M_ord and M ↦ M_nord are exact functors on U-equivariant exact sequences of finite modules.
hypotheses: Exactness in Mathlib's sense Function.Exact f g (range f = ker g).
proofSteps: If x ∈ M_ord and g x = 0, write x = f y; then x = e x = e f y = f e' y ∈ f(M'_ord) (naturality). The reverse inclusion is naturality and g f = 0.
If g is surjective and z ∈ M''_ord, choose g y = z; then g(e y) = e'' g y = z with e y ∈ M_ord.
The ordinary part is a natural direct summand of the identity functor, hence a retract of an exact sequence.
acceptance: No Mittag-Leffler or limit argument enters at finite level.

sources.match: Khare–Thorne prove exactness from the lifted factorisation; naturality gives it directly.

nodes.title: Ordinary parts of quotients
nodes.statement: For M finite as a set, U ∈ End_R(M) and a U-stable submodule P ⊆ M, the ordinary part of M/P for the induced endomorphism is the image of M_ord: (M/P)_ord = (M_ord + P)/P ≅ M_ord/(P ∩ M_ord) = M_ord/P_ord. For a two-sided ideal I of a commutative R and P = IM: (M/IM)_ord = M_ord/I·M_ord and (M/IM)_nord = M_nord/I·M_nord.
hypotheses: P U-stable; for P = IM this holds for every R-linear U when R is commutative.
proofSteps: Apply ordinary-projector-exact to 0 → P → M → M/P → 0.
IM = I·M_ord ⊕ I·M_nord because e_U is R-linear, so (IM)_ord = I·M_ord.
acceptance: Test: M = ZMod 9, U = 3, P = 3M: both sides are 0.

sources.match: Khare–Thorne Lemma 2.10(3), for a proper ideal I.

nodes.title: The ordinary part is the localization at U
nodes.statement: Let R be commutative, M an R-module finite as a set and U ∈ End_R(M); regard M as an R[X]-module with X acting by U (Module.AEval'). Then M_ord → M → M[X⁻¹] = LocalizedModule (powers X) M, x ↦ x/1, is an isomorphism; equivalently the R[X]-linear map M → M_ord, x ↦ e_U x, is a localization at the powers of X (IsLocalizedModule). In particular every U-equivariant map from M to a module on which the endomorphism is bijective kills M_nord.
hypotheses: R commutative (so that R[X] is commutative and LocalizedModule applies).
proofSteps: Injective: if x ∈ M_ord and X^k x = 0 in M then U^k x = 0, so x = 0 since U is injective on M_ord.
Surjective: y/X^k = (U|_{M_ord})^{-k}(e y)/1 + ((1 − e)y)/X^k, and (1 − e)y is killed by U^m, so its fraction vanishes.
Universal property: X acts invertibly on M_ord, and M_nord is X-power torsion.
acceptance: This is the comparison ACC+ use to identify Emerton's localization definition of ordinary parts with the direct-summand definition at finite level.

sources.match: The statement M_ord → M → M ⊗_{O/ϖ^m[U]} O/ϖ^m[U, U⁻¹] is an isomorphism.
ACC+'s remark that the two definitions agree for finitely generated modules.

nodes.title: Finite quotient systems adapted to an endomorphism
nodes.statement: Let M be an R-module and U ∈ End_R(M). A finite quotient system for (M, U) indexed by a set ι is a family (J_i)_{i∈ι} of submodules of M such that: the family is directed downward (for i, j there is k with J_k ⊆ J_i ∩ J_j); each J_i is U-stable; each M/J_i is finite as a set; ⋂_i J_i = 0 (separated); and every compatible family (x_i mod J_i) is represented by one x ∈ M (complete). Then M ≅ lim_i M/J_i, and the J_i form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 for the inverse-limit topology, in which M is compact and U is continuous.
hypotheses: ι arbitrary; the countable case ι = ℕ with J_n decreasing is the one used by Khare–Thorne.
proofSteps: Define the induced endomorphisms U_i of M/J_i by Submodule.mapQ.
Separation and completeness say that the canonical map M → lim M/J_i is bijective.
acceptance: The data are the J_i, not merely a topology: coefficient and level maps must respect them (profinite-projector-natural).

A compact module with a continuous U need not admit a U-stable system: on ∏_{n∈ℕ} ZMod 2 with the left shift, the only U-stable open subgroup is the whole group, and U^{n!} does not converge pointwise.

nodes.title: The profinite ordinary projector
nodes.statement: Let (J_i) be a finite quotient system for (M, U), U_i the induced endomorphisms of M/J_i and e_i = e_{U_i}. There is a unique e = e_U ∈ End_R(M) with e(x) ≡ e_i(x mod J_i) for all i and x. For every x and i, U^{n!}x ≡ e x mod J_i as soon as n ≥ |M/J_i|; thus U^{n!} → e pointwise in the inverse-limit topology. Moreover e² = e, eU = Ue, and e(J_i) ⊆ J_i for all i (continuity).
hypotheses: (J_i) a finite quotient system; no uniform threshold over i is asserted.
proofSteps: For J_k ⊆ J_i the projection M/J_k → M/J_i intertwines U_k and U_i, so it intertwines e_k and e_i (ordinary-projector-natural): (e_i(x mod J_i))_i is a compatible family.
Completeness gives e x; separation gives uniqueness; linearity follows from uniqueness.
U^{n!}x mod J_i = U_i^{n!}(x mod J_i) = e_i(x mod J_i) for n ≥ |M/J_i|.
Idempotence, commutation with U and e(J_i) ⊆ J_i hold modulo every J_k, hence exactly.
acceptance: Pointwise convergence only: for M = ℤ_p and U = p, e = 0 but U^{n!} ≠ 0 for every n.
Independent of the chosen system among systems defining the same topology (projector_unique).

nodes.title: The ordinary decomposition of a profinite module
nodes.statement: With (J_i), e as in profinite-ordinary-projector: M = eM ⊕ (1 − e)M, both summands closed and U-stable; U restricts to a bijection of eM whose inverse is continuous; U is topologically nilpotent on (1 − e)M (for each x there and each i, Uⁿx ∈ J_i for all n large). Conversely e is the only idempotent in End_R(M) commuting with U, preserving every J_i, with U bijective on its range and topologically nilpotent on its kernel.
hypotheses: No uniform exponent: the n in 'Uⁿx ∈ J_i' depends on x only through i (it can be taken |M/J_i|), but U need not be nilpotent on (1 − e)M.
proofSteps: Each summand is the kernel of a continuous endomorphism (1 − e or e), hence closed.

Modulo J_i, U is bijective on e_i(M/J_i) and nilpotent of exponent ≤ |M/J_i| on its complement (ordinary-part-bijective); pass to the limit using completeness for the inverse U^{-1} = lim U^{n!−1} on eM.
Uniqueness: modulo each J_i a competing e' induces a decomposition of M/J_i satisfying the hypotheses of finite-ordinary-decomposition-unique, so e' ≡ e mod J_i for all i.
acceptance: Test on ℤ_p with U = p: (1 − e)M = ℤ_p, U topologically nilpotent but not nilpotent.
Test on ℤ_p² with U = (1 1; 0 p): eM is the line spanned by (1, 0) and (1 − e)M the line spanned by (1, p − 1).

sources.match: The decomposition in the adic case, generalised to finite quotient systems.

nodes.title: Naturality of the profinite projector
nodes.statement: Let (M, U, (J_i)) and (N, V, (K_k)) carry finite quotient systems and let f : M → N be R-linear with fU = Vf and continuous for the systems (for every k there is i with f(J_i) ⊆ K_k). Then f e_U = e_V f. In particular the ordinary part is functorial for level and coefficient maps that respect the quotient systems.
hypotheses: Continuity is the stage's condition 'maps respecting the quotient systems'; an arbitrary R-linear map need not commute with the projectors.
proofSteps: Given k, choose i with f(J_i) ⊆ K_k; f induces M/J_i → N/K_k intertwining U_i and V_k.
By ordinary-projector-natural, f e_U x ≡ e_V f x mod K_k for every k; separation of N gives equality.
acceptance: For finite modules over a complete noetherian local ring every R-linear map is continuous (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/finite-module-inverse-limit), so the hypothesis is automatic in the adic instance.

sources.match: Khare–Thorne Lemma 2.10(2) in the adic case.

nodes.title: Ordinary projectors on finite modules over complete local rings
nodes.statement: Let R be a noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m and finite residue field, M a finite R-module that is m-adically separated and complete (automatic when R is complete), and U ∈ End_R(M). Then (mⁿM)_{n≥0} is a finite quotient system for (M, U). Hence e_U = lim_n U^{n!} exists in End_R(M) for the m-adic topology, is idempotent, M = M_ord ⊕ M_nord with U invertible on M_ord and topologically nilpotent on M_nord, the decomposition is unique and natural for all R-linear maps, and (M/IM)_ord = M_ord/IM_ord for every proper ideal I.
hypotheses: Finite residue field is essential: for R = ℂ (m = 0), M = ℂ and U = 2, the powers 2^{n!} do not converge (finite generation over a complete local ring is not enough).
Topologies: the m-adic topology on End_R(M), equal to the topology of the kernels of End_R(M) → End_R(M/mⁿM).
proofSteps: R/mⁿ is finite (Ideal.finite_quotient_pow with R/m finite) and M/mⁿM is a finite R/mⁿ-module, hence a finite set.

mⁿM is U-stable because U is R-linear; separation and completeness are the m-adic hypotheses, supplied for finite modules over complete noetherian local rings by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/finite-module-inverse-limit.
Convergence in End_R(M): e − U^{n!} maps M into mᵏM once n ≥ |M/mᵏM|, uniformly in x.
Naturality for all R-linear maps: f(mⁿM) ⊆ mⁿN, so profinite-projector-natural applies; the quotient statement is ordinary-projector-quotient at each finite level.
acceptance: Recover Khare–Thorne Lemma 2.10 exactly, including uniqueness and the quotient formula.
Keep the failure test R = ℂ, U = 2 as an explicit non-example of the hypotheses.

sources.match: The standing hypothesis: k is the finite residue field of O.

nodes.title: Inverse limits of exact sequences of finite modules
nodes.statement: Let I be a cofiltered index category and 0 → A_i → B_i → C_i → 0 a natural family of short exact sequences of R-modules with every A_i finite as a set. Then 0 → lim A_i → lim B_i → lim C_i → 0 is exact. More generally, if η : F → G is a natural transformation of functors to sets with every F(i) finite and every η_i surjective, every section of G lifts to a section of F.
hypotheses: Only finiteness of the kernels (hence of the fibres) is needed; no countability of I.
proofSteps: Left exactness of lim is formal.

For c ∈ lim C_i the fibres of B_i → C_i over c_i are nonempty cosets of A_i, hence finite nonempty; they form a cofiltered system of finite nonempty sets, which has a section (nonempty_sections_of_finite_cofiltered_system).
acceptance: This is the compactness form of the Mittag-Leffler argument; for ℕ-indexed towers of artinian modules it agrees with AdicSpacesPartII:F0/mittag-leffler-exactness.

sources.match: Khare–Thorne: systems of finite modules over Artinian quotients satisfy Mittag-Leffler.

nodes.title: Exactness of the profinite ordinary part
nodes.statement: (a) If 0 → M' → M → M'' → 0 is exact, with finite quotient systems on the three modules, continuous U-equivariant maps, then 0 → M'_ord → M_ord → M''_ord → 0 and the non-ordinary sequence are exact. (b) If (0 → M'_c → M_c → M''_c → 0)_c is a cofiltered system of U-equivariant exact sequences of modules finite as sets, then the limit sequence is exact, its terms carry the finite quotient systems given by the kernels of the projections, and (lim M_c)_ord = lim (M_c)_ord.
hypotheses: (b) needs only finiteness of each M'_c (compact surjectivity); for ℕ-indexed towers of artinian modules this is the Mittag-Leffler condition.
proofSteps: (a): e is natural for continuous equivariant maps, so the ordinary sequence is a retract of the given exact sequence.

(b): the limit sequence is exact by finite-inverse-limit-exact; the kernels of lim M_c → M_c form a finite quotient system (separated and complete by construction); the limit projector agrees with the limit of the finite projectors by the uniqueness in profinite-ordinary-projector, and exactness of the ordinary parts at each c passes to the limit by finite-inverse-limit-exact again.
acceptance: State (b) with the actual transition maps; equalities only after taking cohomology do not suffice.

sources.match: Finite-level exactness.
The Mittag-Leffler property of systems of finite modules, used to pass to limits.

nodes.title: Ordinary parts of complexes and their cohomology
nodes.statement: Let C be a complex of R-modules each finite as a set (or finite modules over a noetherian local ring with finite residue field, complete in each degree) and T : C → C a chain endomorphism. The degreewise projectors e_{T^i} form a chain map e_T with e_T² = e_T, giving C = C_ord ⊕ C_nord as complexes; for every i the induced maps give H^i(C_ord) ≅ H^i(C)_ord and H^i(C_nord) ≅ H^i(C)_nord (for the endomorphism H^i(T)); and for a chain map f : C → D with f T = T' f, f(C_ord) ⊆ D_ord and f(C_nord) ⊆ D_nord.
hypotheses: Khare–Thorne print T₂ ∈ End_R(C•) in part 2; the endomorphism of D• is meant (sourceIssues).
In the adic case H^i(C) is a finite R-module, so its ordinary part is defined by adic-instance.
proofSteps: The differentials intertwine T^i and T^{i+1}, so they commute with the projectors (naturality): e_T is a chain map.

Cycles, boundaries and cohomology are obtained from C by kernels and cokernels of equivariant maps; exactness of the ordinary part (finite or adic) identifies Z^i(C_ord) = Z^i(C)_ord, B^i(C_ord) = B^i(C)_ord and H^i(C_ord) = H^i(C)_ord.
acceptance: Degreewise application only uses a chain endomorphism; an endomorphism in the derived category needs derived-ordinary-idempotent.

nodes.title: The ordinary idempotent of an element of a finite algebra
nodes.statement: Let R be a noetherian local ring with finite residue field, A an R-algebra (not necessarily commutative) that is a finite R-module, m-adically complete, and t ∈ A. Then e_t := lim_n t^{n!} exists in A, is the value at 1 of the profinite ordinary projector of left multiplication by t, is an idempotent lying in the R-subalgebra R[t] generated by t, and commutes with every element commuting with t. For an A-module N that is a finite R-module, e_t acts on N as the ordinary projector of t|_N. When A is commutative this is the factorial-powers theorem of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.2 (planned upstream for finite commutative algebras over a complete noetherian local ring with finite residue field); in general it is that theorem applied to the commutative finite R-subalgebra R[t] ⊆ A.
hypotheses: R[t] = Algebra.adjoin R {t}, a finite R-submodule of A, closed and complete by Artin–Rees and Krull.
Applies to A = End_R(M) and A = End_{K(R)}(C) for a good complex C.
proofSteps: R[t] ⊆ A is a commutative R-subalgebra, finite over R because R is noetherian and A is finite; apply IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.2's factorial powers to t ∈ R[t], which gives the idempotent e_t with t^{n!} → e_t in the m-adic topology of R[t].
The topology of R[t] is the subspace topology of A (Artin–Rees), so e_t is also the limit in A; it commutes with every element commuting with t because it is a limit of polynomials in t.
On a finite A-module N, e_t acts as the limit of t^{n!}|_N, which is the profinite ordinary projector of t|_N (L0a/adic-instance).
acceptance: e_t is characterised inside R[t]; an abstract idempotent with the right action on cohomology is not a substitute (stage text).

nodes.title: The ordinary part of a perfect complex
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete noetherian local ring with finite residue field, C a good complex (bounded, with finite projective terms) and t ∈ End_{K(R)}(C) = End_{D(R)}(C). There is a unique idempotent e ∈ End_{K(R)}(C) such that e is a polynomial in t (e ∈ R[t]), H(t) acts invertibly on H(e)H*(C) and topologically nilpotently on (1 − H(e))H*(C); namely e = e_t = lim t^{n!}. For any chain representative T of t, the degreewise ordinary part C_{T,ord} is a direct summand subcomplex whose projection represents e, so e splits in K(R); the resulting C_ord is unique up to isomorphism in K(R), independent of T, and carries x ↦ e x e from any finite R-subalgebra of End_{K(R)}(C) commuting with t. Over an artinian local R this is the telescope comparison of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.2 (ordinary part of a bounded finite complex), which this statement extends to complete R by passing to the limit over R/mⁿ.
hypotheses: C good in Khare–Thorne's sense (§2.2); K(R) is the homotopy category, with End_{K(R)}(C) = End_{D(R)}(C) for good C.
Uses End_{K(R)}(C), a finite R-module since R is noetherian and C has finite projective terms.
proofSteps: End_{K(R)}(C) is a quotient of the finite R-module of chain endomorphisms, hence a finite R-algebra; apply ordinary-idempotent-finite-algebra to t.
For a representative T, e_T (ordinary-part-complexes) is a chain idempotent with e_T = T^{n!} modulo mᵏ for n large, so its class is lim t^{n!} = e: this splits e in K(R).
Properties on cohomology follow from ordinary-part-complexes.
Uniqueness: idempotents of the finite commutative R-algebra R[t] = ∏ R[t]_𝔪 (R complete) correspond to sets of maximal ideals; the cohomological conditions force the set {𝔪 : t ∉ 𝔪}.
acceptance: Do not assume that D(R) is idempotent complete in the library: the splitting is produced from the degreewise ordinary part of a representative.
Record Khare–Thorne's standing hypothesis: R complete noetherian local with finite residue field.

nodes.title: Ordinary parts along a tower of coefficient rings
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete noetherian local ring with finite residue field, I_1 ⊇ I_2 ⊇ … open ideals cofinal with the powers of m, R_c = R/I_c. Suppose given perfect complexes M_c of free R_c-modules, t_c ∈ End_{D(R_c)}(M_c) and morphisms f_{c+1} : M_{c+1} ⊗ R_c → M_c with f_{c+1}(t_{c+1} ⊗ 1) = t_c f_{c+1} inducing isomorphisms H*(M_{c+1} ⊗ R_c)_ord ≅ H*(M_c)_ord. Then there are a minimal complex F_∞ over R and maps g_c : F_∞ ⊗ R_c → M_c, g'_c : M_c → F_∞ ⊗ R_c with g'_c g_c = 1, g_c g'_c the ordinary idempotent of t_c, compatible with the f_c; H*(F_∞ ⊗ R_c) ≅ H*(M_c)_ord. The triple is unique up to an isomorphism unique up to homotopy, and compatible endomorphisms s_c commuting with t_c glue to a unique s_∞ ∈ End_{D(R)}(F_∞).
hypotheses: Cofinality of (I_c) with (mⁿ) is automatic in a complete noetherian local ring (Chevalley); it is stated as a hypothesis here.
Minimal complexes (KT Lemma 2.3) and the gluing of good complexes and homotopy classes along R_c (KT Lemmas 2.13–2.14) are imported from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P7.
proofSteps: Replace each M_c by a minimal complex; choose a chain representative T_c and put F_c = (M_c)_{T_c,ord} with inclusion i_c and projection p_c; then i_c p_c = t_c^{N_c!} in D(R_c).

a_{c+1} = p_c f_{c+1}(i_{c+1} ⊗ 1) : F_{c+1} ⊗ R_c → F_c is a quasi-isomorphism of minimal complexes, hence an isomorphism; glue the F_c to F_∞ with isomorphisms b_c (P7, KT Lemma 2.13) and set g_c = i_c b_c, g'_c = b_c⁻¹ p_c.
H*(F_∞) = lim H*(F_c) by the Milnor sequence, since towers of finite modules over R_c are Mittag-Leffler.
Uniqueness and gluing of s_∞ by the homotopy-class gluing of P7 (KT Lemma 2.13(3)).
acceptance: Keep the ordinary-cohomology compatibility hypothesis; transition maps that are isomorphisms only on the whole cohomology are not required.
The identity g_c g'_c = i_c p_c holds as chain maps, before passing to D(R_c).

nodes.title: Strict neighborhoods with a fixed slope block
nodes.statement: Let r be in the divisible closure of |K×| and let V be an affinoid subdomain of B=Max(R) over which f_r:f_r^{-1}(V)→V is finite of constant degree d>0. Construct an affinoid subdomain X of B that is a strict neighbourhood of V (Buzzard's p. 28 definition: there is a finite union W of affinoid subdomains with V∩W=∅ and X∪W=B) and a radius s>r in the divisible closure of |K×| such that Y=f_s^{-1}(X) contains f_r^{-1}(V), is finite flat of degree d over X, and is open-and-closed in the full spectral preimage f^{-1}(X), so Y lies in the cover C.
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.
R is a reduced K-affinoid algebra with its supremum norm; P(T)=Σ r_n T^n is entire with r_0=1.
r lies in the divisible closure of |K×| and V is an affinoid subdomain of B.
The initial block f_r^{-1}(V)→V is finite of positive constant degree d.
proofSteps: Newton polygons: constant fibre degree d over V means |r_d(x)|≠0 and −log|r_n(x)| ≥ (n−d)log r − log|r_d(x)| for all n, strictly for n>d; use r_0=1 at n=0 to get |r_d(x)| ≥ r^{−d} on V.

Entire decay gives N>d with −log|r_n(x)| > n log(r+1) for n≥N on all of B; the maximum modulus principle on the affinoid V gives t with r<t<r+1 such that −log|r_n(x)| ≥ (n−d)log t − log|r_d(x)| for all n on V, with equality only at n=d.

Choose γ1,γ2,δ1,δ2 in log of the divisible closure of |K×| with log r<γ1<γ2<log t and δ1 < −log|r_d| < δ2 on V. Define X by the N Laurent/rational conditions δ1 ≤ −log|r_d(x)| ≤ δ2; −log|r_n(x)|+log|r_d(x)| ≥ (n−d)γ1 for 0 ≤ n < d (the n=0 condition −log|r_d(x)| ≤ dγ1 is the uniform lower bound for |r_d| on X that the printed range 0<n<d omits); −log|r_n(x)|+log|r_d(x)| ≥ (n−d)log t for d<n<N (printed as (n−d)t). On X the bound |r_d|≥e^{−δ2} makes r_d a unit, so the ratio conditions are Weierstrass conditions inside a Laurent domain and X is an affinoid subdomain.

Strict neighbourhood: V satisfies every defining inequality strictly, so V⊂X. Let W be the union of the affinoid subdomains {|r_d| ≥ e^{−δ1}}, {|r_d| ≤ e^{−δ2}} and, for each ratio condition, {|r_d| ≥ e^{−δ2}} ∩ {reversed ratio inequality}; the intersection with the Laurent domain where r_d is a unit is needed for these pieces to be affinoid subdomains (a bare condition |r_n| ≥ c|r_d| is not an affinoid subdomain at common zeros of r_n and r_d). Then V∩W=∅ and X∪W=B; the manuscript prints X∩W=∅ and X∪V=B, which are the wrong identities.

Set s=exp(γ2). For x∈X and every n≠d one has −log|r_n(x)|+log|r_d(x)| > (n−d)γ2: for 0≤n<d from γ1<γ2, for d<n<N from γ2<log t, and for n≥N from the entire bound together with the n=0 condition (log|r_d(x)| ≥ −dγ1). Hence the Newton polygon of P_x has exactly d roots of norm ≤ s and none of norm s, so f_s^{-1}(X)→X has constant degree d and Corollary 4.3 makes it finite flat.

Y∈C: once Y→X is finite, Y is open and closed in f^{-1}(X) by footnote 2 (Grosse-Klönne; BGR 9.6.3/3 and 9.5.3/5); alternatively make the pointwise 'no root of norm s' uniform on the affinoid X by the maximum modulus principle to obtain an empty annulus s<|T|≤s' over X.
acceptance: Recheck the displayed inequalities against the corrected statement recorded in the gap 'Printed radius and strict-neighbourhood errors': (n−d)log t not (n−d)t; V∩W=∅ and X∪W=B; the n=0 (equivalently δ2<dγ2) lower bound for |r_d| on X; affinoid pieces of W taken inside {|r_d| ≥ e^{−δ2}}.

Test the corrected construction on P(T)=1+uT over B=Sp K⟨u⟩ with V={|u|=1}, r=1, d=1: without the lower bound for |r_d|=|u| the printed X contains points with empty fibre over the disc of radius s, so the degree is not constant.
Prove the finite-flat and open-and-closed conclusions from the corrected inequalities, keeping radii and logarithmic radii distinct.

nodes.title: An admissible cover by finite slope blocks
nodes.statement: The affinoid domains Y of Z that are finite surjective over an affinoid weight domain and open-and-closed in its full spectral preimage form an admissible cover of Z.
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.
R is a reduced K-affinoid algebra with its supremum norm.
proofSteps: For each truncated Z_r, filter the base by the finite degree-at-least-i loci U_i of Lemma 4.4 (each a finite union of affinoids, U_{i+1}⊆U_i, empty for large i).

Start with the maximal-degree locus U_d: cover it by affinoids V_α, where the degree is exactly d, so Corollary 4.3 gives finite flatness; enlarge each block to a strict neighbourhood X_α with Y_α=f_{s_α}^{-1}(X_α) by Lemma 4.5.

Descend by induction on i: from a witness W with W∩U_i=∅ and W∪⋃X_α=B, cover W∩U_{i−1} (a finite union of affinoids on which the degree is exactly i−1) by new blocks, apply Lemma 4.5 to them, and intersect witnesses to keep a strict-neighbourhood witness for U_{i−1}.

Coverage of f_r^{-1}(U_{i−1}) needs, for the old blocks, f_r^{-1}(X_α)⊆Y_α, which holds because s_α>r; record this in the induction hypothesis H(i), since the printed H(i) only records f_r^{-1}(U_i)⊆⋃Y_α and the printed step ends without checking coverage of points of U_{i−1}∖U_i lying in some X_α.
Conclude that every Z_r is covered by finitely many selected affinoids; since Y∩Z_r is an affinoid subdomain of the affinoid Z_r, the cover is admissible.
acceptance: Establish a finite cover on each Z_r, not merely coverage of geometric points.
Keep the strict-neighborhood induction and the finite-flatness theorem as explicit prerequisites.

sources.match: The source proves admissibility by finite covers of each truncation and descending degree induction.

nodes.title: A polynomial for each spectral block
nodes.statement: For a connected affinoid weight domain A and a finite-flat spectral block Y of degree d, identify O(Y) with A[T]/(Q₀), normalize Q₀ to have constant term one, and obtain a coprime factor Q of the Fredholm series. Apply the Riesz theorem to obtain the associated finite projective Hecke-stable summand N.
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.
R is a reduced K-affinoid algebra with its supremum norm.
Y belongs to the admissible slope cover.
proofSteps: Take the characteristic polynomial Q_0 (monic of degree d) of the spectral coordinate T acting on the finite projective module O(Y) over the connected affinoid A=O(X); Cayley–Hamilton gives A[T]/(Q_0)→O(Y).

Use the closed immersion of Y in X×B[0,r] and the equivalence of residue and finite-module Banach norms (BGR 3.7.4/1) to prove that A[T]/(Q_0)→O(Y) is surjective; equal ranks make it an isomorphism, so F_A vanishes in A{{T}}/(Q_0) and Q_0 divides F_A.

Normalise Q=a_0^{-1}Q_0 with Q(0)=1 and unit leading coefficient. The source invokes Theorem 3.3 without arguing that Q is coprime to S:=F_A/Q. Supply it: Y is open and closed in f^{-1}(X), so over each point x the roots of Q_x are the roots of F_x lying in Y_x with their full multiplicities; hence S_x has no root in common with Q_x, Res(Q,S) has no zero on Max(A), so it is a unit in the affinoid A and (Q,S)=1 by the resultant-unit criterion.
Apply the exact finite-slope theorem to obtain N with Q*(φ)=0 on N; the projector lies in the closure of A[φ], so N is stable under the commuting Hecke algebra.
acceptance: Prove Q(0)=1 and a unit leading coefficient, and justify coprimality with the complementary factor.

Prove coprimality of Q with the cofactor S explicitly (the source omits it); test on a chart whose fibre over some point has a root of F_x of multiplicity 2 to see why the open-and-closed property is what guarantees full multiplicities in Q_x.
Keep N finite projective; a global basis is not part of the conclusion.

sources.match: The source derives the slope polynomial from O(Y) and invokes Theorem 3.3 with projective, not free, output.

uses.how: the finite projective summand N carries the Hecke action.
Q* has unit constant term, so φ is invertible on N by a polynomial.

nodes.title: Flat base change of eigenvarieties
nodes.statement: For a flat morphism R→R′ of reduced affinoid algebras, the eigenvariety formed after completed scalar extension agrees with the pullback eigenvariety. The spectral hypersurface commutes with arbitrary continuous coefficient extension, but the same assertion for the Hecke-image algebra requires a separate argument.
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.

R→R′ is flat for the eigenvariety comparison.
proofSteps: Lemma 5.4: the spectral variety commutes with any continuous base change by Lemma 2.13.

Pull back the admissible finite-slope cover: for Y∈C its pullback Y′ lies in C′; the pulled-back blocks form an admissible cover of Z_{φ′} because finitely many of them cover each pulled-back truncation Z′_r (the source's appeal to BGR 9.1.4/2 for the separated space Z_{φ′} supplies affinoidness of intersections, not admissibility by itself).

Use flatness of R→R′ to commute taking the finite Hecke image inside End_A(N) with coefficient extension; without flatness the natural map from D(Y′) to the pullback of D(Y) need not be an isomorphism.
Glue the finite-chart comparisons along the pulled-back cover.

nodes.title: Radius changes and linked Banach modules
nodes.statement: A primitive link α:M′→M with compact Hecke-equivariant c:M→M′ satisfying αc=φ and cα=φ induces an isomorphism of eigenvarieties. Finite composites of primitive links have the same property.
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.
R is a reduced K-affinoid algebra with its supremum norm.
M and M′ satisfy (Pr) and carry the same commuting Hecke actions.
proofSteps: Use the cyclic determinant identity (Lemma 2.12; the proof on p. 40 cites Lemma 2.13 for this step, which is the base-change lemma, while p. 39 correctly cites Lemma 2.12) to identify the Fredholm hypersurfaces and hence the slope covers C and C′.
On every slope block, φ is invertible on N and N′ by a polynomial ψ(φ) in R[φ] because Q* has unit constant term.
Show ψ(φ)c is a two-sided inverse to α:N′→N on the finite projective summands (α and c commute with φ, so they respect the kernels of Q*(φ)); transport their Hecke-image algebras and glue.
acceptance: Require genuine intertwining identities for a radius change; equality of pointwise eigenvalues is insufficient.
Check compatibility with all chart-gluing maps.

nodes.title: The eigenvariety over weight space
nodes.statement: For a reduced rigid weight space W with (Pr) Banach modules on its affinoids, compact controlling operators, commuting Hecke actions and compatible links under restriction, glue the affinoid constructions to a rigid eigenvariety over W.
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.
W is a reduced rigid space; for each admissible affinoid open X⊆W, R_X=O(X) with its supremum norm carries a (Pr) Banach module M_X with a commuting action of T and compact φ_X.

For affinoid opens X_i⊆X_j there are links α_{ij}: M_{X_i} → M_{X_j} ⊗̂_{O(X_j)} O(X_i) with the cocycle α_{13} = (α_{23} ⊗̂ 1) ∘ α_{12} for X_1⊆X_2⊆X_3. The printed display 'α_ij: M_{X_i} → M_{X_i} ⊗̂_{O(X_i)} O(X_j)' on p. 41 is mis-indexed; the corrected typing above is the one used in the proof of Construction 5.7.
proofSteps: Compare the module on a smaller affinoid with the base extension of the module on a larger one using the link theorem.
Use flat affinoid base change to compare their eigenvarieties.
Apply the compatibility of the links to verify descent and glue over W.
acceptance: Prove canonical restriction to every affinoid and independence of the covering.
Do not infer reducedness or flatness over W from reducedness of W.

nodes.title: Points and finite-slope eigenpackets
nodes.statement: Identify L-points of the constructed eigenvariety with φ-finite simultaneous Hecke eigensystems in the completed coefficient fibers, for complete extensions L/K. This classifies eigensystems, not a unique eigenvector or its multiplicity.
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.
R is a reduced K-affinoid algebra with its supremum norm.
proofSteps: Reduce to K-points: the source asserts that separatedness of D_φ lets one base extend to L; the base change of the whole construction along R_X→R_X⊗̂_K L must be justified (it is a flat base change of reduced affinoids, so Lemmas 5.4–5.5 apply), which the source leaves implicit.
Reduce to a finite projective slope module N over an affinoid chart Y with base X∋P; K-points of D(Y) above P are K-algebra maps from T(Y)/mT(Y) to K.

For a residue specialization compare T(Y)/mT(Y) with its image S in End_K(N/mN); Lemma 5.10 proves the kernel is nilpotent by Cayley–Hamilton on matrices whose entries lie in m, so both have the same prime ideals, and a K-valued character of the commutative algebra S has a common eigenvector in N/mN.

Conversely an eigenvector m∈M_X⊗̂K with λ(φ)≠0 gives a point (P,λ(φ)^{-1}) of Z_φ (1−λ(φ)^{-1}φ is not injective, so by Lemma 3.1 over K the Fredholm series vanishes there); choose Y∈C containing it; then Q*_P(λ(φ))=0 and Q*(φ) is invertible on the specialised complement, so m lies in N⊗K. The source states the reduction to N⊗K without this argument.
acceptance: Retain the distinction between the point classification and an isomorphism of possibly nonreduced specialized Hecke algebras.
Check that the controlling eigenvalue is nonzero.
Write out the two directions of the bijection separately; the source's one-sentence reduction to N⊗K and its base-change remark are not proofs.

sources.match: The nilpotent-kernel argument explains why eigenpackets can specialize correctly even when the full algebra does not commute with base change.

nodes.title: Equidimensionality and components of the eigenvariety
nodes.statement: If the reduced weight space W is equidimensional of dimension n, then the eigenvariety D_φ of Construction 5.7 is equidimensional of dimension n, and each irreducible component of D_φ maps finitely and surjectively onto an irreducible component of the spectral variety Z_φ. Under Chenevier's additional identification of the components of Z_φ, those are Fredholm hypersurfaces cut out by prime Fredholm series and their images in W are Zariski open in components of W.
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; the data of Construction 5.7 with every affinoid X⊆W reduced and equidimensional of dimension n.
Irreducible components of rigid spaces are taken in the sense of Conrad, Irreducible components of rigid spaces (Ann. Inst. Fourier 49, 1999), which is imported unread.
The description of the components of Z_φ as prime Fredholm hypersurfaces uses Coleman–Mazur Theorem 1.3.11 over power-series rings, or Conrad's 4.3.2, and is not proved for an arbitrary reduced W.
proofSteps: For a chart Y∈C with connected base X=Max(A), the Hecke image T(Y) is a commutative A-subalgebra of End_A(N) with N finite projective, hence T(Y) is A-torsion-free after every flat base change (Chenevier, Lemme 6.2.10, first assertion).

A finite A-algebra that is torsion-free after flat base change has every irreducible component of its spectrum mapping surjectively onto an irreducible component of Spec A, so it is equidimensional of dimension n when A is (Lemme 6.2.10, second and third assertions; the proof localises at the image of a minimal prime and uses that the fibre is discrete and that a torsion-free quotient forces the image prime to be minimal).

Apply this to A ⊂ A[φ^{-1}] ⊂ T(Y): the affinoid Y has O(Y)=A[T]/(Q) whose map to A[φ^{-1}] is a nil-isomorphism (Lemme 6.4.3: the characteristic polynomial ideal satisfies I^r⊂(P)⊂I), so Y, Max A[φ^{-1}] and D(Y) share equidimension n, and π and the projection to X send components to components.

Glue: an irreducible component Σ of D_φ meets each D(Y) in a union of components (Conrad 2.2.9), its image π(Σ) is an irreducible closed analytic subset of Z_φ (Conrad 2.2.3) of dimension n, hence a component of the n-equidimensional Z_φ (Conrad 2.2.7).

Buzzard's Lemma 5.8 states this result for the general machine and delegates the proof to Chenevier's Proposition 6.4.2; the argument above uses only T(Y)⊂End_A(N) and equidimensionality of the charts, so the delegation is legitimate in Buzzard's generality once the imported component theory is available.
acceptance: State the torsion-freeness and equidimensionality lemma as a purely algebraic statement about finite algebras over Noetherian rings and test it on A=K⟨X,Y⟩ with the nonreduced example of Buzzard p. 33, where T(Z_φ)=R⊕I is finite and torsion-free.
Do not claim the Zariski-density statement for images of components without the Fredholm-series factorisation input (Coleman–Mazur 1.3.11 or Conrad 4.3.2).

sources.locator: Lemma 5.8 and its one-line proof, p. 41
sources.match: Buzzard states equidimensionality, surjectivity onto components of Z_φ and Zariski-density of images and delegates the entire proof to Chenevier.
The proof reduces equidimensionality to the algebraic lemma applied to the Hecke image inside End of the finite projective slope module, which is exactly the structure available in Buzzard's machine.

This is the algebraic input: subalgebras of End_A(N) for projective N are torsion-free, and finite torsion-free algebras over equidimensional Noetherian rings are equidimensional with components mapping onto components.
The nil-isomorphism between O(Y) and A[φ^{-1}] and the Zariski-open image statement.

nodes.title: The nearly ordinary weight algebra of a totally real field
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real of degree d, p odd, U ⊆ GL₂(𝒪_F ⊗ Ẑ) open compact with U_v = GL₂(𝒪_{F,v}) for v | p, and 𝒪 the ring of integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p. Put U^f = U ∩ A_f^×, Z(U_a) = U^f·𝒪_F^×/U^f_a·𝒪_F^× and Z(U) = lim_a Z(U_a); G(U_a) ≅ (𝒪_F/p^a)^× × Z(U_a) via (a b; c d) ↦ (∏_{v|p}(a^{−1}d)_v, a), and G(U) = lim_a G(U_a) ≅ (𝒪_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× × Z(U). Z(U) has a maximal ℤ_p-free direct summand of rank δ_F, the ℤ_p-rank of the Galois group of the maximal abelian pro-p extension of F unramified outside p, generated by the reciprocity images x_1, …, x_{δ_F} of elements γ_i^{p^{r_i}}; for each v_i | p the units 𝒰_{v_i} ≡ 1 mod v_i have a free summand of rank d_i = [F_{v_i} : ℚ_p] generated by y^{(i)}_1, …, y^{(i)}_{d_i}. The weight algebra is Λ′_𝒪 = 𝒪[[X_1, …, X_{δ_F}, Y^{(i)}_j]] (δ_F + d variables), and 𝒪[[G(U)]] is a finite free Λ′_𝒪-module through 1 + X_i ↦ x_i, 1 + Y^{(i)}_j ↦ y^{(i)}_j, of rank the index of the closed subgroup H these generate. Its weight-two arithmetic points are the kernels of Λ′_𝒪 → Q̄_p with 1 + Y^{(i)}_j ↦ φ(y^{(i)}_j) and 1 + X_i ↦ ψ(x_i) for finite-order characters φ of (𝒪_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× and ψ of Z(U); they are Zariski dense in Spec Λ′_𝒪.
hypotheses: p odd; U maximal at p. δ_F = 1 + the Leopoldt defect of (F, p) by class field theory.
proofSteps: G(U) ≅ (𝒪_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× × Z(U): the map is well defined on U⁰_a·A_f^× modulo U_a·𝒪_F^× and bijective by the definitions (Skinner–Wiles p. 32).

Z(U) is (𝒪_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× modulo the closure of the global units, times a finite prime-to-p part; its ℤ_p-rank is d − rank(closure of 𝒪_F^×) = 1 + δ, which by class field theory is the rank of the maximal abelian pro-p extension unramified outside p.
H ≅ ℤ_p^{δ_F + d} has finite index in G(U), so 𝒪[[G(U)]] ≅ Λ′_𝒪[G(U)/H] is finite free over Λ′_𝒪 = 𝒪[[H]] (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1).
Density: in each variable the kernels of 1 + X ↦ ζ (ζ a p-power root of unity) are infinitely many height-one primes; products of such give a Zariski-dense set in Spec Λ′_𝒪.
acceptance: The X-variables see only the ℤ_p-free part of Z(U); the torsion of G(U) (roots of unity, the finite quotient by global units) is not a weight variable.
Nearly ordinary weight space includes the torus (Y) directions; the ordinary one-variable weight space of L0 is the parallel, untwisted slice.

nodes.title: Hida's freeness theorem for definite quaternionic forms
nodes.statement: (Skinner–Wiles Proposition 3.3, after Hida [H2, Theorem 3.8].) Let F have even degree, with the definite quaternionic towers M_∞(U), M⁺_∞(U) of L5/ordinary-towers-duality. If every element of U/(U ∩ F^×) acts on D^×\G^D(A_f) without fixed points, then M_∞(U) and M⁺_∞(U) are projective 𝒪[[G(U)]]-modules, hence free Λ′_𝒪-modules, of rank rank_𝒪(M_∞(U) ⊗_{Λ′_𝒪} 𝒪). When the ordinary parts have the same 𝒪-rank on the factors of 𝒪[G(U_a)] belonging to all characters of the torsion of G(U), this rank is rank_𝒪 eH⁰(X(U⁰_1), 𝒪) × #G(U)_tors, as Skinner–Wiles state (E11).
hypotheses: [F : ℚ] even; the fixed-point-free hypothesis on U/(U ∩ F^×).
proofSteps: Free action: #X(U_a) = #X(U⁰_a)·#G(U_a) and H⁰(X(U⁰_a), K/𝒪) = H⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪)^{G(U_a)}, so the Pontryagin dual of H⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪) is free over 𝒪[G(U_a)] of rank #X(U⁰_a) (R18.3).

e commutes with G(U_a), so the dual of eH⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪) is a direct summand, hence projective over 𝒪[G(U_a)]; for b ≥ a its coinvariants under ker(G(U_b) → G(U_a)) are the level-a module, by the free action.

Level independence (eH⁰(X(U⁰_a), K/𝒪) = eH⁰(X(U⁰_1), K/𝒪), OAFML R21.1) bounds the number of generators, so M_∞(U) = lim_a of these duals (OAFML R21.1/ordinary-towers-duality) is finitely generated projective over 𝒪[[G(U)]].

𝒪[[G(U)]] is finite free over the local ring Λ′_𝒪 (totally-real-weight-algebra), so M_∞(U) is projective, hence free, over Λ′_𝒪; the same argument applies to the dual of eH⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪)⁺ and M⁺_∞(U).
acceptance: Downstream (hida-hecke-finite; OAFML R21.2 Lemmas 3.10 and 3.19) only freeness over Λ′_𝒪 is used.
The step Skinner–Wiles call clear (drop e) gives projectivity, not freeness of constant rank over 𝒪[G(U_a)] (E11).

nodes.title: Finiteness of the nearly ordinary Hecke algebra over Λ′
nodes.statement: (Skinner–Wiles Corollary 3.4.) Let F have even degree. For every U, T_∞(U, 𝒪) is a finite torsion-free Λ′_𝒪-module; in particular it is a semilocal ring complete for its radical, the product of its localisations at its finitely many maximal ideals.
hypotheses: [F : ℚ] even.
proofSteps: Choose a prime ℓ ∤ 6 unramified in F such that V = U ∩ U(ℓ) acts freely modulo F^× (Skinner–Wiles Lemma 3.5, requested from R18.3).
Pullback H⁰(X(U_a)) → H⁰(X(V_a)) is injective and commutes with the traces in a, so M_∞(U) ↪ M_∞(V), compatibly with T_∞(V, 𝒪) → T_∞(U, 𝒪); hence it is a map of Λ′_𝒪-modules.
M_∞(V) is free of finite rank (hida-freeness), so M_∞(U) is finite and torsion-free over the Noetherian Λ′_𝒪.

T_∞(U, 𝒪) acts faithfully on M_∞(U) (each T₂(U_a, 𝒪) acts faithfully on eH⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪)⁺, dual to its level-a quotient), so T_∞(U, 𝒪) ↪ End_{Λ′_𝒪}(M_∞(U)) is finite and torsion-free; finite over the complete local Λ′_𝒪 makes it semilocal and complete.
acceptance: No freeness of T_∞(U, 𝒪) over Λ′_𝒪 is claimed; only M_∞(V) is free.

nodes.title: Hida's control theorem for nearly ordinary Hilbert forms
nodes.statement: (Skinner–Wiles Proposition 3.7, Hida [H2, Corollary 2.5].) Let F have even degree. If λ : T_∞(U, 𝒪) → Q̄_p is an 𝒪-algebra homomorphism with λ|_{Z(U)} = ψε^μ, μ ≥ 0, where ψ and φ = λ|_{(𝒪_F⊗ℤ_p)^×} have finite order, then there is a nearly ordinary cuspidal automorphic representation π of parallel weight k = (μ + 2)·t such that λ(T(ℓ)) and λ(S(ℓ)) are the T(ℓ)- and S(ℓ)-eigenvalues of the newform of π for every prime ℓ ∤ p with U_ℓ = GL₂(𝒪_{F,ℓ}). The kernels of such λ are the algebraic primes of weight k.
hypotheses: [F : ℚ] even; ε is the cyclotomic character, viewed on Z(U) through reciprocity Z(U) → Gal(F^{(p)}/F).
proofSteps: For μ = 0 the statement is the weight-two correspondence: λ factors through some T₂(U_a, 𝒪) by the definition of T_∞, and T₂(U_a, 𝒪) acts on the v-good vectors of π ∈ Π^{n.o.}_2(U_a) (Skinner–Wiles p. 37).
For μ > 0 Skinner–Wiles cite Hida [H2, Corollary 2.5] without proof; the proof is recorded as a gap.
acceptance: Weights are parallel here: the torus character φ has finite order. Non-parallel weights need λ|_{torus} algebraic, which Proposition 3.7 does not treat.

nodes.title: Weight-two algebraic primes are dense on every component
nodes.statement: (Skinner–Wiles Lemma 3.8 and Corollary 3.9.) Let Q be a minimal prime of T_∞(U, 𝒪) and 𝒳(Q) the set of algebraic primes of weight 2 containing Q. Then 𝒳(Q) is Zariski dense in Spec(T_∞(U, 𝒪)/Q). Consequently, if V ⊇ U and for all P in a Zariski-dense subset of 𝒳(Q) some λ ∈ ℋ(P) factors through T_∞(U, 𝒪) → T_∞(V, 𝒪), then Q is the inverse image of a minimal prime of T_∞(V, 𝒪).
hypotheses: [F : ℚ] even; ℋ(P) is the finite set of λ with kernel P.
proofSteps: T_∞(U, 𝒪)/Q is a domain, finite and torsion-free over Λ′_𝒪 (hida-hecke-finite), so Λ′_𝒪 ↪ T_∞/Q is a finite injective extension and Spec(T_∞/Q) → Spec Λ′_𝒪 is surjective (lying over).
Every prime of T_∞/Q over a weight-two arithmetic point of Λ′_𝒪 is the kernel of some λ with finite-order restrictions, hence algebraic of weight 2 (hida-control-nearly-ordinary with μ = 0).

The weight-two points of Λ′_𝒪 are dense (totally-real-weight-algebra). If the closure of 𝒳(Q) were a proper closed subset of the irreducible Spec(T_∞/Q), its image would be a closed subset of smaller dimension containing a dense set, which is impossible.

Corollary 3.9: the λ factoring through T_∞(V, 𝒪) on a dense set put Q inside the closed set cut out by ker(T_∞(U) → T_∞(V))-compatible primes; a minimal prime of T_∞(V, 𝒪) below a generic point pulls back to Q.
acceptance: Skinner–Wiles call the density 'immediate' after the Λ′_𝒪 statement; the lying-over and dimension step is spelled out here.

nodes.title: The ordinary family modular-symbol module M_m
nodes.statement: Let p be odd, N prime to p, T*_N (resp. T_N) Hida's universal ordinary Hecke algebra of tame level N acting on all (resp. cuspidal) forms, and m a maximal ideal of T*_N whose residual representation ρ̄_m is irreducible. For each r ≥ 0 the relative homology sequence 0 → H₁(X₁(Np^r); ℤ_p) → H₁(X₁(Np^r), C₁(Np^r); ℤ_p) → H̃₀(C₁(Np^r); ℤ_p) → 0 (4.1) remains exact on ordinary parts, and after localising at m the reduced H₀ of the cusps vanishes. So M_m := lim_r H₁(X₁(Np^r); ℤ_p)^ord_m ≅ lim_r H₁(X₁(Np^r), cusps; ℤ_p)^ord_m is a module over (T*_N)_m ≅ (T_N)_m. Complex conjugation on X₁(Np^r) commutes with the Hecke action, and M_m = M⁺_m ⊕ M⁻_m.
hypotheses: p odd (for the ± splitting); ρ̄_m irreducible (so the cusps disappear after localisation and (T*_N)_m = (T_N)_m).

nodes.title: Freeness of M^±_m: the family period line
nodes.statement: (Emerton–Pollack–Weston Proposition 4.1.1.) If ρ̄_m is irreducible and p-distinguished, each of M⁺_m and M⁻_m is a free (T_N)_m-module of rank one.
hypotheses: ρ̄_m irreducible and p-distinguished (the two characters of ρ̄_m|_{G_{ℚ_p}} are distinct).
proofSteps: Wiles [34, Theorem 2.1] with Theorem 2.1.2: J₁(Np)(ℚ̄)[m]^ord is free of rank 2 over T_N/m (requested from ModularCurvesPartII R14.6).
By (4.2), Hom(M_m, ℚ_p/ℤ_p)[m] ≅ H₁(Np; ℚ_p/ℤ_p)^ord_m[m] ≅ H₁(Np; F_p)^ord_m[m] ≅ J₁(Np)[p][m]^ord, so M_m/mM_m is free of rank 2 over T_N/m.
M_m ⊗ ℚ_p is free of rank 2 over (T_N)_m ⊗ ℚ_p (Eichler–Shimura in each weight), so Nakayama makes M_m free of rank 2, and the ± parts are free of rank 1.
acceptance: Without p-distinguishedness M^±_m need not be free; the family period is then a module, not a line.

nodes.title: Family periods as trivialisations of an invertible module
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of family-symbol-free-rank-one, a family period for the sign ± is an isomorphism θ^± : (T_N)_m ≅ M^±_m (4.3); two choices differ by a unit of (T_N)_m. At a classical height-one prime ℘ of (T_N)_m, θ^± mod ℘ is a generator of the saturated integral period lattice of the eigenform f_℘ (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L1), so the single choice θ^± fixes the canonical periods of all f_℘ up to the units of the O(℘), compatibly along the family.
hypotheses: ρ̄_m irreducible and p-distinguished.
proofSteps: θ^± exists by freeness; Aut_{T_m}(M^±_m) = T_m^×.
Reduction mod ℘ and control identify M^±_m/℘ with the ±-part of the classical symbols of f_℘ with 𝒪(℘)-coefficients, free of rank one; its generator is the saturated lattice generator of MS L1.
acceptance: A period line is not a globally chosen basis: θ^± is data, and statements depending on it are equalities up to T_m^× (integrally) or up to O(℘)^× at ℘, not up to a field scalar.
Where M^±_m is not free (p-distinguishedness fails) only the module, not a trivialisation, is available.

nodes.title: The two-variable measure of a Hida family
nodes.statement: The paths [∞, a] on X₁(Np^r), a ∈ P¹(ℚ), give classes in H₁(X₁(Np^r), cusps; ℤ_p) compatible in r; projecting to ordinary parts, localising at m and passing to the limit gives a ↦ {∞, a} ∈ M_m. For a + p^rℤ_p ⊆ ℤ_p^×, µ(a + p^rℤ_p) := U_p^{−r}{∞, a/p^r} ∈ M_m (Definition 4.1.2) is additive (Proposition 4.1.3), hence defines L(m, N) ∈ M_m ⊗̂_{ℤ_p} ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]], with ± components L^±(m, N) ∈ M^±_m ⊗̂ ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]]; after a family period it lies in (T_N)_m[[ℤ_p^×]]. Projecting to the ω^i-part gives L(m, N, ω^i) ∈ (T_N)_m ⊗̂ Λ^{(i)} with sign (−1)^i (the other sign projects to 0).
hypotheses: ρ̄_m irreducible; U_p is invertible on M_m (ordinary part).
proofSteps: Additivity: U_p = Σ_{b mod p}(1 b; 0 p) acts on {∞, a/p^r} as Σ_b {∞, (a + bp^r)/p^{r+1}}, so µ(a + p^rℤ_p) = Σ_b µ(a + bp^r + p^{r+1}ℤ_p).
ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]] is the ring of ℤ_p-valued measures (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1); the completed tensor product uses the m-adic topology on M_m.
The sign of the ω^i-projection: the involution z ↦ −z on ℤ_p^× corresponds to complex conjugation.
acceptance: U_p^{−r} makes sense because U_p is a unit on the ordinary part; this is where ordinarity is used.
L(m, N) is integral: no denominators are introduced before a period is chosen.

nodes.title: Specialisation to one-variable p-adic L-functions
nodes.statement: (Emerton–Pollack–Weston Proposition 4.1.4.) Under the hypotheses of family-symbol-free-rank-one, for every classical height-one prime ℘ of (T_N)_m, L^±(m, N)(℘) ∈ O(℘)[[ℤ_p^×]] is the analytic p-adic L-function of the normalised eigenform f_℘ ∈ S_k(Np^∞, O(℘))^ord[κ_℘], computed with respect to a canonical period; f_℘ need not be new, so the specialisation may be imprimitive (Euler factors at primes dividing the tame level of an oldform removed).

proofSteps: The one-variable construction µ_{r,k}(a + p^nℤ_p) = U_p^{−n}{∞, a/p^n} ∈ (M_{r,k})_{m_{r,k}} gives L^±_p(m_{r,k}, N).
(M_{r,k})^±_{m_{r,k}} is free of rank one over (T_{r,k})_{m_{r,k}} by control and family-symbol-free-rank-one; the family period induces its trivialisation.

By construction L^±(m, N) ≡ L^±(m_{r,k}, N) mod ω_{r,k}, hence mod ℘; reduction of the latter mod ℘_{r,k} is the p-adic L-function of f_℘ for the canonical period (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L2's ordinary integral measure).
