nodes.title: Locally finite endomorphisms of complete modules
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m and finite residue field, and let M be an R-module that is m-adically separated and complete (M ≅ lim_n M/mⁿM; no finiteness of M is assumed). An R-linear endomorphism T of M is locally finite if for every n ≥ 1 and every v ∈ M/mⁿM the R-submodule of M/mⁿM spanned by the orbit {T^k v : k ≥ 0} is finitely generated; equivalently, each M/mⁿM is the directed union of its T-stable finitely generated R-submodules. Since R/mⁿ is finite, a finitely generated R/mⁿ-module is a finite set, so each such submodule is finite.
hypotheses: R complete noetherian local with finite residue field; M m-adically separated and complete; T ∈ End_R(M).
proofSteps: The two formulations agree: the span of an orbit is T-stable, and a sum of finitely many T-stable finitely generated submodules is again one.
A finitely generated R/mⁿ-module is finite as a set because R/mⁿ has finite length and finite residue field (Ideal.finite_quotient_pow).
acceptance: A finite R-module carries only locally finite endomorphisms; the notion is new only for modules that are not finitely generated, such as completed direct sums of copies of R or completed cohomology.

sources.match: Defines local finiteness on m_R-adically separated complete modules by finite generation of orbit spans modulo every power of m_R, and restates it as M/mⁿ being an inductive limit of finite T-stable modules.
The same definition, phrased as: each M/mⁿ is an inductive limit of finite type T-stable submodules.

nodes.title: Stability of local finiteness under extensions, quotients and products
nodes.statement: Let 0 → M₁ → M₂ → M₃ → 0 be an exact sequence of m-adically separated complete R-modules with compatible endomorphisms T. (1) If T is locally finite on M₁ and M₃, it is locally finite on M₂. (2) If T is locally finite on M₂, it is locally finite on M₃. (3) If T is locally finite on M₂ and mⁿM₂ = 0 for some n, it is locally finite on M₁. Without the bounded-torsion hypothesis (3) fails: on M₂ = ∏_{i≥0} ℤ_p with T(a_0, a_1, …) = (0, p a_0, p² a_1, …, p^i a_{i−1}, …), T is locally finite on M₂ and preserves the kernel M₁ of M₂ → ∏_i ℤ/p^{(i+1)²}, but is not locally finite on M₁. (4) If T₁, T₂ commute and are locally finite on M, then T₁T₂ is locally finite.
hypotheses: R complete noetherian local with finite residue field; all modules m-adically separated and complete; T-equivariant maps.
proofSteps: (1): modulo mⁿ, write the image M of M₁/mⁿ in M₂/mⁿ; T is locally finite on M by (2). Given v, local finiteness on M₃ gives T^N v = w + Σ_{i<N} a_i T^i v with w ∈ M, and local finiteness on M gives a relation for w; the span of {T^i v, T^j w} is T-stable and finitely generated.
(2) and (3) are immediate from the definition, since an orbit span in a submodule killed by mⁿ is an orbit span in M₂/mⁿ.

The counterexample: elements of M₁ have coordinates divisible by growing powers of p, and modulo p the orbit of a suitable element of M₁ has infinitely many independent images (Pilloni's Remark 2.1.1).
(4): reduce to M killed by mⁿ; the span of {T₂^i T₁^j v} is finitely generated and T₁T₂-stable.
acceptance: The counterexample of (3) is checked as stated: T maps M₂ into the kernel M₁ and fails local finiteness there, so no stability under arbitrary submodules is claimed.

sources.match: Parts (1)–(3) with the proof of (1), and the product-of-ℤ_p counterexample showing that (3) needs the bounded-torsion hypothesis.

nodes.title: Local finiteness is detected modulo the maximal ideal
nodes.statement: For an m-adically separated complete R-module M and T ∈ End_R(M), T is locally finite on M if and only if the induced endomorphism of M/mM is locally finite.
hypotheses: R complete noetherian local with finite residue field; M m-adically separated and complete.
proofSteps: Necessity is part (2) of L0a/locally-finite-stability.

Sufficiency by induction on n, using the right exact sequence (m^{n−1}/mⁿ) ⊗_R M → M/mⁿM → M/m^{n−1}M → 0: the left term is a quotient of a finite direct sum of copies of M/mM (m^{n−1}/mⁿ is a finite-dimensional R/m-space), so T is locally finite on it and on its image, and part (1) of L0a/locally-finite-stability applies to the image and the quotient.
acceptance: For M = ℤ_p^{(ℕ)} completed and T the shift, the criterion fails modulo p, matching not_isLocallyFiniteEnd_shift.

nodes.title: The ordinary projector of a locally finite endomorphism
nodes.statement: Let T be a locally finite endomorphism of an m-adically separated complete R-module M. For every v ∈ M the sequence T^{N!}v converges m-adically; e(T)v := lim_N T^{N!}v defines an R-linear idempotent e = e(T) ∈ End_R(M) commuting with T, and M = eM ⊕ (1 − e)M with both summands T-stable and closed, T bijective on eM and topologically nilpotent on (1 − e)M (for each v ∈ (1 − e)M and each n, Tᵏv ∈ mⁿM for k large). e is the unique idempotent with these properties. When every M/mⁿM is finite, e coincides with the projector of L0a/profinite-ordinary-projector for the quotient system (mⁿM)_n.
hypotheses: T ∈ End_R(M) locally finite (L0a/locally-finite-action).
proofSteps: Fix n and v ∈ M/mⁿM; the orbit span V of v is a finite T-stable module, so L0a/finite-ordinary-projector gives T^{N!}v = e_V v for N ≥ |V|, independent of the choice of V by L0a/ordinary-projector-natural applied to inclusions of finite T-stable submodules.
The resulting projectors on the M/mⁿM are compatible in n (naturality for the reduction maps), and m-adic completeness assembles them into e on M.

Bijectivity of T on eM, topological nilpotence on (1 − e)M and uniqueness are checked modulo each mⁿ on finite T-stable submodules, where they are L0a/ordinary-part-bijective and L0a/finite-ordinary-decomposition-unique.
acceptance: No uniform exponent N with e = T^{N!} on all of M is asserted; on the diagonal example of L0a/locally-finite-action, e is the projection onto the e_0-coordinate and T^{N!} differs from it at every finite N.

sources.match: Existence and uniqueness of e = lim T^{N!} with the decomposition, proved by reduction to a finite R/mⁿ-module where the factorial powers are eventually constant.

nodes.title: Functoriality and exactness of locally finite ordinary parts
nodes.statement: Let f : M₁ → M₂ be a T-equivariant R-linear map of m-adically separated complete modules on which T is locally finite. (1) f e = e f, so f(eM₁) ⊆ eM₂ and f((1 − e)M₁) ⊆ (1 − e)M₂. (2) If M₃ = coker f is m-adically separated and complete, coker(eM₁ → eM₂) = eM₃. (3) If T is locally finite on M₀ = ker f, then ker(eM₁ → eM₂) = eM₀.
hypotheses: T locally finite on M₁ and M₂ (and on M₀ for (3)); the cokernel separated and complete for (2).
proofSteps: Since f commutes with T, it commutes with each T^{N!}, hence with their limit e (continuity of f for the m-adic topologies).
Thus f is the direct sum of ef and (1 − e)f, which gives (2) and (3); T is locally finite on M₃ by L0a/locally-finite-stability (2).
acceptance: For the inclusion pℤ_p → ℤ_p with T = multiplication by a unit, both ordinary parts are everything and the cokernel ℤ/p is its own ordinary part.

sources.match: Naturality of the projector and its compatibility with cokernels and kernels, from the decomposition of f.

nodes.title: Locally finite endomorphisms of complete flat complexes
nodes.statement: Let C^flat(R) be the category of bounded complexes of flat m-adically separated complete R-modules and D^flat(R) the full subcategory of D(R) of objects they represent (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P7, complete flat complexes). A chain endomorphism T of M• ∈ C^flat(R) is locally finite if it is locally finite on every term Mⁱ; then the degreewise projectors form a chain idempotent e(T). An endomorphism T of an object M• of D^flat(R) is locally finite if it has a representative (M•₀, T₀) with M•₀ ∈ C^flat(R) and T₀ a locally finite chain endomorphism. Characterisation (Pilloni Proposition 2.3.1): T is locally finite if and only if it admits some representative in C^flat(R) and acts locally finitely on every Hⁱ(M• ⊗^L_R R/m).
hypotheses: R complete noetherian local with finite residue field.
proofSteps: Degreewise projectors commute with the differentials because the differentials are T-equivariant (L0a/locally-finite-projector-exactness (1)).
Characterisation, forward direction: Hⁱ(M•₀ ⊗ R/m) is a subquotient of Mⁱ₀/m, so L0a/locally-finite-stability applies.

Converse: replace a representative M•₀ by a minimal complete flat subcomplex N• that is a deformation retract (differentials zero modulo m), using the splitting of a complete flat map into an isomorphism and a part vanishing modulo m; the transferred endomorphism s T₀ i acts on Nⁱ/m = Hⁱ(M• ⊗ R/m) as T does, hence is locally finite by L0a/locally-finite-mod-maximal.
acceptance: On a perfect complex every endomorphism is locally finite (Remark 2.3.1), so the notion adds nothing in D^perf(R) and is needed only for complexes of non-finitely-generated complete flat modules.

nodes.title: The ordinary direct factor of a locally finite derived endomorphism
nodes.statement: Let T be a locally finite endomorphism of M• ∈ D^flat(R). A locally finite representative (M•₀, T₀) gives the chain idempotent e₀ = e(T₀) and the direct factor ē₀M• of M• in D(R) represented by e₀M•₀. If ē₀M• lies in D^perf(R), then for any other locally finite representative (M•₁, T₁), ē₁M• also lies in D^perf(R) and the canonical map ē₀M• → ē₁M• is a quasi-isomorphism; the ordinary direct factor e(T)M• ∈ D^perf(R) is therefore well defined up to canonical isomorphism, although the idempotent itself is only defined on representatives. When M• is perfect it agrees with the Khare–Thorne ordinary part of L0a/derived-ordinary-idempotent.
hypotheses: T locally finite on M• ∈ D^flat(R); ē₀M• perfect for one representative.
proofSteps: On each Hⁱ(M• ⊗^L R/m) the operators T₀ and T₁ induce the same locally finite endomorphism; by L0a/locally-finite-projector-exactness the projectors induced by e₀ and e₁ both equal its ordinary projector there, so ē₀M• → ē₁M• is an isomorphism modulo m.
ē₁M• is perfect because its reduction modulo m has finite cohomology (complete flat complexes with finite residual cohomology are perfect).
A map of complete flat complexes that is a quasi-isomorphism modulo m is a quasi-isomorphism.
On a perfect M• the endomorphism algebra is finite over R and the factorial-power idempotent is unique (Pilloni Remark 2.3.1), which identifies the construction with L0a/derived-ordinary-idempotent.
acceptance: The statement asserts independence of the direct factor up to canonical quasi-isomorphism, never equality of idempotents in End_{D(R)}(M•) for non-perfect M•.

sources.locator: §2.3, Lemma 2.3.2 and the paragraph after it, pp. 10–11; Remark 2.3.1, p. 11
sources.match: Independence of the direct factor from the representative under the perfectness hypothesis, the warning that the projector may depend on the representative, and compatibility with Khare–Thorne Lemma 2.12.
Restates the independence statement and adopts the abuse of notation e(T).

nodes.title: Ordinary projectors over complete semilocal coefficient rings
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete semilocal noetherian ring whose quotient by its Jacobson radical is finite (for example Λ = ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]] for odd p, a product of p − 1 complete local rings ℤ_p[[1 + pℤ_p]]). Then R = ∏_j R_j with each R_j complete local with finite residue field, every R-module M decomposes as ∏_j M_j, and an endomorphism T is locally finite when each component T_j is; the ordinary projector, the derived ordinary direct factor and their properties are defined factor by factor, with 'perfect' read as 'bounded complex of finite projective R-modules' (finite projective modules over R need not be free when the factors have different ranks).
hypotheses: R complete semilocal noetherian with R/rad(R) finite.
proofSteps: A complete semilocal ring is the product of its localisations at its maximal ideals (idempotent lifting along the radical); IHG.2's finite local factors give the decomposition for finite algebras over a complete local base.
All constructions of L0a/locally-finite-ordinary-projector and L0a/derived-ordinary-direct-factor commute with finite products.
acceptance: For R = ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]] the decomposition has exactly p − 1 factors, indexed by the characters of μ_{p−1}.

sources.locator: §2 (standing hypothesis that R is complete local, p. 7) applied to Λ = ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]] in Parts II–IV
sources.match: Pilloni states §2 for complete local R and applies it to the semilocal weight algebra; the factor-by-factor reading is recorded as an issue in the extraction of the paper.

nodes.title: Characteristic polynomials of endomorphisms of finite projective modules
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, V a finite projective A-module of constant rank d and f ∈ End_A(V). The characteristic polynomial Q_f(X) := D(1 − X f) ∈ A[X] is the value of the degree-d determinant law of the finite projective A[X]-module A[X] ⊗_A V at 1 − X·(1 ⊗ f); it has constant term 1 and degree at most d, its leading coefficient is (−1)^d det f, it commutes with base change A → A′, it agrees with det(1 − X M) for the matrix M of f in any basis when V is free, and it satisfies Cayley–Hamilton in the reciprocal form X^d Q_f(1/X)|_{X = f} = 0 in End_A(V).
hypotheses: V finite projective of constant rank d (Module.rankAtStalk constant).
proofSteps: The determinant law of a finite projective constant-rank module is IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.0 (top exterior power is invertible, endomorphisms of it are scalars, glued from local trivialisations).
Base change of the law and its agreement with Matrix.det on a basis give the formula det(1 − X M) on free modules and the comparison with Mathlib's LinearMap.charpoly (charpoly f = X^d Q_f(1/X)).

Cayley–Hamilton holds Zariski-locally on Spec A, where V is free (LinearMap.aeval_self_charpoly), hence globally since End_A(V) embeds in the product of its localisations; alternatively it is the Cayley–Hamilton identity for the determinant law.
acceptance: This closes the earlier gap 'Characteristic polynomials over finite projective modules'; slope-polynomials uses Q_f.

sources.match: Takes the characteristic polynomial of the controlling operator on a finite projective A-module of rank d, monic of degree d after reversal, with Cayley–Hamilton; this node supplies that object, which Mathlib defines only for free modules.

nodes.title: The spectral hypersurface of a compact endomorphism of a complex
nodes.statement: Let A be a reduced affinoid algebra over a complete non-archimedean field K ⊇ ℚ_p, M• a bounded complex of projective Banach A-modules (direct summands of orthonormalisable ones) and U ∈ End_{K^proj(A)}(M•) compact, i.e. represented by a chain endomorphism Ũ that is compact in every degree. The characteristic series P̃(X) = ∏_k det(1 − X Ũ | M^k) is an entire series over A (the product, not the alternating product, so that every eigenvalue in every degree is seen). Its zero locus Z̃ ⊆ Sp(A) × A¹ carries a complex of coherent sheaves 𝓜• (the universal generalised eigenspace complex of Ũ): Z̃ has an admissible cover by affinoids Y finite and flat over their image V ⊆ Sp(A), with Y a union of connected components of Z̃ ×_{Sp A} V, and on such Y the complex 𝓜•|_Y is the finite slope subcomplex of M•|_V cut out by the factor of P̃ attached to Y, a perfect complex of O(V)-modules.
hypotheses: A reduced affinoid; M• bounded with projective Banach terms; Ũ compact in each degree.
proofSteps: In each degree apply the Fredholm theory of compact operators on projective Banach modules (LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4); the characteristic series of the complex is the product of the degreewise ones.

The admissible cover by finite flat spectral blocks is L2a/admissible-slope-cover applied to P̃; on a block the Riesz factorisation P̃ = Q·S gives Ũ-stable decompositions Mᵏ = N_Q(Mᵏ) ⊕ F_Q(Mᵏ) compatible with the differentials, and the finite slope subcomplex N_Q(M•) is a bounded complex of finite projective O(V)-modules (LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4, the finite-slope subcomplex and its perfect model).
𝓜•|_Y is N_Q(M•) viewed over O(Y) = O(V)[X]/(Q) with X acting as Ũ⁻¹; the identifications glue by the compatibility of Riesz projectors under refinement.
acceptance: For a complex concentrated in one degree the construction is L2a/spectral-hypersurface.

sources.match: For a compact endomorphism of a bounded complex of projective Banach modules, the product characteristic series, the spectral variety Z̃ it cuts out, the universal eigenspace complex over it and the cover by opens finite over their images on which it is perfect.

nodes.title: The spectral variety of a compact endomorphism in the homotopy category
nodes.statement: With M•, U and a compact representative Ũ as in L2a/complex-spectral-hypersurface, the cohomology sheaves 𝓗ⁱ(𝓜•) are coherent on Z̃. Let 𝓘 ⊆ O_{Z̃} be the annihilator of the graded module ⊕_i 𝓗ⁱ(𝓜•). The spectral variety of (M•, U) is the closed subspace Z = V(𝓘) ⊆ Z̃, with the graded coherent sheaf 𝓗•(𝓜•) supported on it. Z and 𝓗•(𝓜•) on Z depend only on U ∈ End_{K^proj(A)}(M•), not on the representative Ũ; the cohomology sheaves have slope decompositions, and at a rank-one point x of Sp(A) the fibre cohomology Hⁱ(M•_x) has slope decompositions for U.
hypotheses: As in L2a/complex-spectral-hypersurface.
proofSteps: Coherence: on a block, 𝓗ⁱ(𝓜•) is the cohomology of a bounded complex of finite O(Y)-modules.

Independence of Ũ: two compact representatives are homotopic through a compact homotopy; on any finite slope window the finite slope subcomplexes are homotopy equivalent (LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4, homotopy invariance on a slope window), so their cohomology sheaves are isomorphic over the common blocks and the annihilators agree.
The extra components of Z̃ coming from a contractible summand (as in the cone test) carry zero cohomology and are removed in Z.
acceptance: Local constancy of x ↦ Σ_i (−1)ⁱ dim Hⁱ(M•_x)_{=h} on rank-one points is LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4/finite-slope-euler-local-constancy, cited, not replanned; the neighbourhoods need not cover Sp(A) (Pilloni's footnote 20).

sources.match: Defines Z as the vanishing locus of the annihilator of the cohomology of the universal eigenspace complex, states its independence of Ũ, and proves local constancy of the slope-h Euler characteristic at rank-one points from that of the degreewise slope-h dimensions.

Defines the spectral variety of U as the support of the cohomology sheaves, independent of the representative, and deduces local constancy of the slope-zero Euler characteristic over classical weights from Coleman's theory.

nodes.title: The coherent eigenmodule sheaf on an eigenvariety
nodes.statement: In the setting of L2a/global-weight-gluing (reduced rigid weight space W, linked (Pr) Banach modules, compact controlling operator φ, commuting Hecke algebra 𝐓), the finite projective slope summands N(Y) of the spectral blocks Y, viewed as T(Y)-modules, glue to a coherent sheaf 𝓜 on the eigenvariety D with 𝓜(D(Y)) = N(Y). It is torsion-free over W when W is, its formation commutes with flat base change of the weight space, and for a point w of W and a point x of D over w with residue field L, the fibre 𝓜 ⊗ k(w) at x is the generalised eigenspace (M_w ⊗ L)^{≤h}[x] of the specialised Banach module. The map 𝐓 ⊗ k(w) → End(𝓜 ⊗ k(w)) has image the Hecke algebra of the fibre, and the surjection from the fibre of O_D at w onto it has nilpotent kernel; D is not asserted reduced, and the nilpotents of the fibre algebra are retained.
hypotheses: The data of L2a/global-weight-gluing; slopes bounded on each chart.
proofSteps: On a chart D(Y) = Sp T(Y), the module N(Y) is finite projective over A and a faithful T(Y)-module, hence a coherent sheaf on D(Y).
Under refinement of blocks and restriction of affinoids, the Riesz projectors are compatible (L2a/hecke-chart-gluing), giving gluing data for the N(Y).

Fibres: Riesz decompositions commute with specialisation (LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4 completed base change), so N(Y) ⊗ k(w) is the slope part of the fibre; localising at x gives the generalised eigenspace.
Nilpotent kernel: T(Y) ⊗ k(w) and the Hecke algebra of the fibre act faithfully on modules with the same semisimplification, so the kernel consists of nilpotent elements (Chenevier's lemma).
acceptance: This answers the earlier gap 'Coherent eigenmodules and nonflat specialization' for the eigenmodule itself; Tor terms for cohomology in several degrees are the complex version, L2a/complex-spectral-variety.

The specialisation of the Hecke algebra of a finite slope family maps onto the Hecke algebra of the fibre with nilpotent kernel.
Uses Chenevier's lemma in the modular-symbol case: the specialisation map of Hecke algebras is surjective with nilpotent kernel.

nodes.title: Families of locally analytic distributions over an affinoid of weight space
nodes.statement: Let W = Sp R be an affinoid subdomain of the weight space 𝒲 of continuous characters of ℤ_p^×, with universal character κ_W : ℤ_p^× → R^×. For r ∈ p^ℤ, r ≤ 1, let A[r] be the affinoid algebra of the closed neighbourhood {z ∈ ℂ_p : |z − a| ≤ r for some a ∈ ℤ_p} of ℤ_p, with sup norm, and D[r] its continuous dual. The completed tensor products R ⊗̂ A[r] and R ⊗̂ D[r] are orthonormalisable Banach R-modules with R ⊗̂ D[r] = Hom_R(R ⊗̂ A[r], R); for r₁ > r₂ the restriction R ⊗̂ A[r₁] → R ⊗̂ A[r₂] and the dual map R ⊗̂ D[r₂] → R ⊗̂ D[r₁] are compact. The monoid Σ₀(p) of integral matrices (a b; c d) with p ∤ a, p | c and ad − bc ≠ 0 acts on R ⊗̂ A[r] by (γ·f)(z) = κ_W(a + cz) f((b + dz)/(a + cz)) and dually on R ⊗̂ D[r]; for every w ∈ W(ℚ_p) the specialisation along w : R → ℚ_p identifies these with A_w[r] and D_w[r] carrying the weight-w action.
hypotheses: W = Sp R ⊆ 𝒲 an affinoid inside one component, so that κ_W(a + cz) is an analytic function of z on the residue discs (after shrinking, R = ℚ_p⟨T⟩ and κ_W(x) = ω(x)^i ⟨x⟩^T).
proofSteps: Orthonormalisability: norms of elements of A[r] lie in |ℚ_p^×| when r ∈ p^ℤ, so A[r] and D[r] are orthonormalisable (Serre), and completed tensor products with R stay so.
Compactness of the restriction maps between radii is the classical compactness of restriction of affinoid functions to a strictly smaller disc.
κ_W(a + cz) ∈ R ⊗̂ A[1] because log((a + cz)/ω(a)) ∈ pA[1]; this defines the action and its specialisation is the weight-w action of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L2.
acceptance: At integral weights the specialised action is the weight-k action of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L2, so the classical distribution modules are recovered.

nodes.title: Families of distribution-valued modular symbols with compact U_p
nodes.statement: Let N ≥ 1 be prime to p and Γ = Γ₁(N) ∩ Γ₀(p). For W = Sp R and r as in L2/distribution-families, Symb_Γ(R ⊗̂ D[r]) = Hom_Γ(Δ₀, R ⊗̂ D[r]) (Δ₀ the degree-zero divisors on P¹(ℚ)) is a Banach R-module with Buzzard's property (Pr) (through a finite presentation of Δ₀ as a ℤ[Γ]-module by Manin relations, which exhibits it as a closed submodule of a finite direct sum of copies of R ⊗̂ D[r] cut out by finitely many continuous relations). The Hecke operators T_ℓ (ℓ ∤ Np), the diamond operators and U_p act continuously, the involution ι = diag(−1, 1) splits it into ± parts, U_p is compact, and for w ∈ W(ℚ_p) there is a Hecke- and ι-equivariant specialisation map Symb^±_Γ(R ⊗̂ D[r]) ⊗_{R,w} ℚ_p → Symb^±_Γ(D_w[r]), which Bellaïche asserts is an isomorphism (Proposition 3.3(iii)); its kernel and cokernel are the Tor terms of the universal-coefficients comparison for H¹_c (E14), and the planned statement keeps them.
hypotheses: N prime to p; W an affinoid in one component of weight space; r ∈ p^ℤ with 0 < r ≤ 1.
proofSteps: The Manin-relations presentation of Δ₀ (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L0, the coset description) identifies Symb_Γ(A) with the kernel of an A-linear map A^a → A^b given by an integral matrix in ℤ[Σ₀(p)]; for A = R ⊗̂ D[r] this is a closed submodule, and (Pr) follows as in Pollack–Stevens's treatment of overconvergent symbols. Bellaïche's own route through (10) is defective (E14).
Compactness of U_p: it factors through the symbols with values in R ⊗̂ D[r/p] followed by the compact radius change.

Base change: the presentation commutes with flat base change (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L0/symbols-base-change); along the non-flat specialisation w the comparison map is the degree-one edge map of the universal-coefficients spectral sequence for compactly supported cohomology, whose correction terms are Tor terms; this is the specialisation statement with its Tor terms that the stage requires.
acceptance: U_p is compact on the family module, and the specialisation map is stated with its Tor terms; that it is an isomorphism (Bellaïche Proposition 3.3(iii)) is the source's claim, whose proof through (10) is recorded as E14.

sources.match: Modular symbols with values in a module with Σ₀(p)-action, their Hecke operators and involution, the finite-orbit description, and Proposition 3.3: property (Pr), continuity, compactness of U_p and specialisation.

nodes.title: Finite slope pieces of family modular symbols
nodes.statement: For ν > 0 and W = Sp R small enough that the Fredholm series of U_p on Symb^±_Γ(R ⊗̂ D) has a slope-ν factorisation, the Riesz decomposition gives a U_p- and Hecke-stable direct summand Symb^±_Γ(R ⊗̂ D)^{≤ν}, finite projective over R, on which U_p is invertible with generalised eigenvalues of valuation ≤ ν. Its formation commutes with specialisation: for w ∈ W(ℚ_p), Symb^±_Γ(R ⊗̂ D)^{≤ν} ⊗_{R,w} ℚ_p ≅ Symb^±_Γ(D_w)^{≤ν} Hecke-equivariantly. It is independent of r ≤ 1, because U_p-finite slope parts do not see the radius change.
hypotheses: (W, ν) adapted: the slope-ν factorisation exists over R (always after shrinking W).
proofSteps: Riesz theory for compact operators on (Pr) modules (Coleman, Serre, Buzzard), from LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4.
Specialisation: Riesz decompositions commute with base change along w (LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4 completed base change and uniqueness of slope decompositions).
Independence of r: the radius-change maps are compact injections commuting with U_p and induce isomorphisms on finite slope parts.
acceptance: The rank of the slope-≤ν piece equals the dimension of every fibre, as the specialisation isomorphism requires.

nodes.title: Local pieces of the modular-symbol eigencurve
nodes.statement: For an adapted pair (W, ν), let 𝕋^±_{W,ν} be the R-subalgebra of End_R(Symb^±_Γ(R ⊗̂ D)^{≤ν}) generated by the Hecke operators T_ℓ (ℓ ∤ Np), U_p and the diamond operators. It is finite and torsion-free, hence flat, over the one-dimensional affinoid algebra R (a principal ideal domain after shrinking W), and C^±_{W,ν} := Sp 𝕋^±_{W,ν} is an affinoid with a finite flat weight map κ^± : C^±_{W,ν} → W. Each Hecke operator is a bounded function on C^±_{W,ν}, and U_p is invertible with valuation ≤ ν. The point-wise version 𝕋^±_{w,ν} ⊆ End_{ℚ_p}(Symb^±_Γ(D_w)^{≤ν}) has ℚ̄_p-points the Hecke eigensystems occurring in Symb^±_Γ(D_w)^{≤ν}.
hypotheses: (W, ν) adapted; W one-dimensional and connected.
proofSteps: Finiteness: a subalgebra of the endomorphisms of a finite projective module over a noetherian ring.
Torsion-freeness: it acts faithfully on a torsion-free module; flatness over the Dedekind ring R follows.
This is L2a/finite-hecke-images in the modular instance, with the controlling operator φ = U_p.
acceptance: κ^± is finite and flat, and the ℚ̄_p-points over w are the eigensystems of the fibre (with L2/specialisation-nilpotent-kernel).

nodes.title: Specialisation of Hecke algebras has nilpotent kernel
nodes.statement: For every w ∈ W(ℚ_p), the specialisation map s_w : 𝕋^±_{W,ν} ⊗_{R,w} ℚ_p → 𝕋^±_{w,ν}, compatible with the Hecke operators, is surjective with nilpotent kernel. Hence the ℚ̄_p-points of the fibre (κ^±)⁻¹(w) are in bijection with the Hecke eigensystems in Symb^±_Γ(D_w)^{≤ν}, and localising at such a point x gives a surjective local map s_x : (𝕋^±_{W,ν})_{(x)} ⊗_{R(w)} ℚ̄_p → (𝕋^±_{w,ν})_{(x)} of finite local ℚ̄_p-algebras with nilpotent kernel. The fibre algebra and the Hecke algebra of the fibre are not identified.
hypotheses: (W, ν) adapted; w ∈ W(ℚ_p).
proofSteps: Surjectivity: the image is a subalgebra of 𝕋^±_{w,ν} containing the image of the Hecke operators.

Nilpotent kernel: both algebras act faithfully, through the specialisation isomorphism of L2/family-slope-pieces, on modules with the same semisimplification; an element acting by zero on Symb(D_w)^{≤ν} is nilpotent on the fibre of the family module (Chenevier, Lemme 6.6), which is the content of L2a/coherent-eigenmodule-sheaf.
acceptance: At a point where κ^± is étale and the generalised eigenspace is one-dimensional, s_x is an isomorphism ℚ̄_p → ℚ̄_p.

sources.match: The specialisation map from the fibre of the family Hecke algebra to the Hecke algebra of the fibre is surjective with nilpotent kernel (citing Chenevier, Lemme 6.6), giving a bijection on points and a surjection of local rings at each point.
The general statement for finite slope families.

nodes.title: The eigencurves C^± from overconvergent modular symbols
nodes.statement: Gluing the local pieces C^±_{W,ν} over an admissible cover of weight space by adapted pairs (L2a's eigenvariety machine with the Banach modules Symb^±_Γ(R ⊗̂ D) over the affinoids of 𝒲, the compact operator U_p and the Hecke algebra generated by T_ℓ (ℓ ∤ Np), U_p and the diamond operators) gives rigid spaces C^± of tame level Γ₁(N) with a weight map κ^± : C^± → 𝒲 and analytic functions T_ℓ, U_p on C^± (U_p invertible). C^± is equidimensional of dimension one, κ^± is locally finite and flat, and for every complete extension L/ℚ_p the L-points of C^± over w ∈ 𝒲(L) are the systems of Hecke eigenvalues of finite slope in Symb^±_Γ(D_w) ⊗ L.
hypotheses: N prime to p; weight space 𝒲 of continuous characters of ℤ_p^× (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L0a).
proofSteps: Construct the local pieces (L2/local-eigencurve-piece) and glue them along restriction and refinement (L2a/hecke-chart-gluing and L2a/global-weight-gluing), the linked Banach modules being the family symbols for nested affinoids.
Points: L2a/eigenpacket-points combined with L2/specialisation-nilpotent-kernel.
Equidimensionality and flatness: each local piece is finite flat over a one-dimensional affinoid, so every component has dimension one.
acceptance: Every refined newform of slope < k + 1 gives a point (L2/small-slope-classicality), and the eigencurve is equidimensional of dimension one.

The evaluation and specialisation maps of family symbols are maps of coherent sheaves; 𝓢^± is not asserted to be locally free at every point, and an eigenpacket is not identified with a unique eigenvector.

nodes.title: Classicality of small-slope points of the eigencurve
nodes.statement: Let x be a point of C^± over an integral weight k ≥ 0 with v_p(U_p(x)) < k + 1. Then the specialisation ρ*_k : Symb^±_Γ(D_k) → Symb^±_Γ(V_k) restricts to an isomorphism of generalised eigenspaces at x, Symb^±_Γ(D_k)(x) ≅ Symb^±_Γ(V_k)(x), and x is the eigensystem of a classical p-stabilised form of weight k + 2 and level Γ (cuspidal, or an Eisenstein series of the sign of the ± part). Classical points of slope < k + 1 are Zariski dense in every component of C^±, and accumulate at every classical point of small slope.
hypotheses: x over k ∈ ℤ_{≥0}; slope strictly less than k + 1.
proofSteps: Stevens' control theorem (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L2) gives the isomorphism on slope-<k+1 parts; restrict to the x-generalised eigenspace (L2/eigensymbol-sheaf).
Eichler–Shimura (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L0) identifies Symb^±_Γ(V_k) with weight-(k + 2) forms of level Γ, so x is classical.

Density: on a local piece over W, the integral weights k with k + 1 > ν are dense in W, and every component of C^±_{W,ν} is finite flat over W, so its points over those weights are classical and Zariski dense.
acceptance: The slope bound is strict: at slope exactly k + 1 (critical slope) ρ*_k need not be injective on the eigenspace; that case is PadicFamilies L3.

sources.match: Stevens' control theorem in slope < k + 1, the Eichler–Shimura isomorphism for modular symbols with its ± split and boundary symbols, and the resulting Hecke embeddings into classical forms whose images contain the cusp forms.

nodes.title: Freeness of family symbols at étale non-critical points
nodes.statement: Let x ∈ C^± lie over an integral weight k with slope < k + 1, corresponding to a refined newform f_β whose generalised eigenspace Symb^±_Γ(V_k)(f_β) is one-dimensional, and assume κ^± is étale at x. Then the localisation of 𝓢^± at x is free of rank one over the local ring O_{C^±,x}, and O_{C^±,x} ≅ O_{𝒲,k}; consequently, after shrinking, there is a neighbourhood V of x and a family symbol Φ ∈ 𝓢^±(V) whose specialisation at every classical point y ∈ V is a generator of the eigenline of y. This is the local freeness hypothesis required to form scalar-valued families of p-adic L-functions.
hypotheses: x classical of slope < k + 1; newform eigenspace of dimension one; κ^± étale at x.
proofSteps: The fibre of 𝓢^± at x is Symb^±_Γ(D_k)(x) ≅ Symb^±_Γ(V_k)(x) (L2/small-slope-classicality), of dimension one.
𝓢^± is torsion-free over the discrete valuation ring O_{𝒲,k}, and O_{C^±,x} = O_{𝒲,k} by étaleness, so 𝓢^±_x is free and its rank is the fibre dimension, by Nakayama's lemma.
A generator over a neighbourhood specialises to a nonzero element of each one-dimensional classical eigenline nearby (the eigenspaces are one-dimensional at nearby classical newform points).
acceptance: The hypotheses are visible: at a critical point with e > 1 the fibre has dimension e and the statement fails, which is L3/family-symbols-free-rank-one's setting.

sources.match: At points where the weight map is étale, the slope-bounded family symbols localised at the point form a free module of rank one over the local Hecke algebra; the critical (non-étale) case is treated separately there and in PadicFamilies L3.

nodes.title: Comparison with the Coleman–Mazur–Buzzard eigencurve
nodes.statement: Let C be the Coleman–Mazur–Buzzard eigencurve of tame level Γ₁(N) built from Coleman's Banach modules of overconvergent modular forms, and C⁰ ⊆ C its cuspidal closed subspace. There are canonical closed immersions C⁰_{W,ν} ↪ C^±_{W,ν} ↪ C_{W,ν} compatible with the weight maps and Hecke functions, and for integral k the semisimplified slope-≤ν Hecke modules satisfy S†_{k+2}(Γ)^{ss} ⊆ Symb^±_Γ(D_k)^{ss} ⊆ M†_{k+2}(Γ)^{ss}; in particular the generalised eigenspaces of a cuspidal refined form have the same dimension in S† and in Symb^±.
hypotheses: N prime to p; the overconvergent-forms eigencurve C as constructed by Coleman–Mazur (N = 1, p > 2) and Buzzard (general N).
proofSteps: Chenevier's comparison theorem for eigenvarieties: two reduced equidimensional eigenvarieties over 𝒲 whose classical structures (Zariski-dense sets of classical points with the same Hecke eigensystems) correspond are related by closed immersions.
The classical structures match by Coleman's control theorem on overconvergent forms and Stevens' control theorem with Eichler–Shimura on symbols (L2/small-slope-classicality).
acceptance: The overconvergent-forms side (Coleman's Banach modules and his control theorem) and Chenevier's comparison theorem are recorded gaps: no roadmap plans Coleman's overconvergent elliptic modular forms; the modular-symbol eigencurve C^± is self-contained without them.

nodes.title: The congruence module of an augmentation
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, O an integral domain and λ : A → O a surjective ring homomorphism with kernel 𝔭_λ. For an ideal J of A and an A-module M write M[J] = {m ∈ M : Jm = 0}, and put I_λ := A[𝔭_λ] = Ann_A(𝔭_λ). The congruence module of M at λ is the O-module Ψ_λ(M) := M / (M[𝔭_λ] + M[I_λ]) (it is killed by 𝔭_λ + I_λ, hence an O/λ(I_λ)-module). It is functorial in A-linear maps, and when A is noetherian local, λ local, O a complete discrete valuation ring and A ⊗ Frac(O) is reduced at 𝔭_λ (A in the category C_O(0) of Iyengar–Khare–Manning), Ψ_λ(M) is a torsion O-module of finite length that agrees, for M of positive depth, with their higher-codimension congruence module Ψ_A(M) in codimension zero.
hypotheses: λ : A → O surjective onto a domain; M any A-module.
proofSteps: Functoriality: an A-linear map sends M[J] into M'[J] for every ideal J.

Torsion and finite length when A is regular at 𝔭_λ in codimension zero: after inverting a uniformiser, A ⊗ K splits as K × B with 𝔭_λ and I_λ generating the unit ideal, so M[𝔭_λ] + M[I_λ] has full rank.

Comparison with Iyengar–Khare–Manning: their Proposition 2.10 gives a natural surjection from M/(M[𝔭_λ] + M[I_λ]) onto their Ψ_A(M) with torsion kernel, bijective when depth_A M ≥ 1; their Example 2.11 shows it can fail to be injective in depth zero.

nodes.title: The congruence ideal of an augmentation
nodes.statement: For λ : A → O as in L1/congruence-module, the congruence ideal is η_λ := λ(I_λ) = λ(Ann_A(𝔭_λ)) ⊆ O. If A is reduced and finite flat over a domain base mapping onto O compatibly (for example A finite flat over O, or a reduced finite flat Λ-algebra and λ onto a branch), then Ann_A(I_λ) = 𝔭_λ and Ψ_λ(A) ≅ O/η_λ; for A finite flat over a complete discrete valuation ring O and reduced, η_λ is nonzero and O/η_λ is finite.
hypotheses: λ : A → O surjective; for the identification Ψ_λ(A) ≅ O/η_λ, A reduced with Ann_A(I_λ) = 𝔭_λ.
proofSteps: Ψ_λ(A) = A/(I_λ + Ann_A(I_λ)) = A/(I_λ + 𝔭_λ) ≅ O/λ(I_λ).
In a reduced ring the annihilator of the annihilator of a minimal-prime-type ideal 𝔭_λ returns 𝔭_λ when A ⊗ K = K × B with 𝔭_λ the kernel of the first projection.
acceptance: For the fibre product of two copies of ℤ_p glued modulo pⁿ, η_λ = pⁿℤ_p and Ψ_λ(A) ≅ ℤ/pⁿ.

nodes.title: The reduced Hida algebra T_Σ of a residual representation and its branches
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(k) be irreducible, odd, ordinary, p-distinguished and modular, with a chosen p-stabilisation, N(ρ̄) its tame conductor, and for a finite set Σ of primes ℓ ≠ p let N(Σ) = N(ρ̄)∏_{ℓ∈Σ} ℓ^{m_ℓ} with m_ℓ = dim V^{I_ℓ}. T_Σ = T_Σ(ρ̄) is the localisation of the ordinary Hecke algebra T′_{N(Σ)} (without U_ℓ for ℓ | N(Σ)) at the unique maximal ideal whose residual representation with its p-stabilisation is ρ̄; it is reduced and finite flat over Λ, carries ρ_Σ : G_ℚ → GL₂(T_Σ) with trace ρ_Σ(Frob_ℓ) = T_ℓ for ℓ ∤ N(Σ)p, and Σ ⊆ Σ′ gives a surjection T_{Σ′} → T_Σ. For a minimal prime 𝔞 of T_Σ, T(𝔞) := T_Σ/𝔞 is a local domain finite over Λ; there are a unique divisor N(𝔞) of N(Σ) and a minimal prime 𝔞′ of the new quotient T^new_{N(𝔞)} over 𝔞, and T(𝔞) ↪ T(𝔞)° := T^new_{N(𝔞)}/𝔞′ is an isomorphism after inverting p (and an isomorphism when N(𝔞) = N(ρ̄)).
hypotheses: ρ̄ irreducible, odd, ordinary, p-distinguished and modular; p ≥ 5 is not needed for the definitions.
proofSteps: Existence and uniqueness of the maximal ideal: modularity of ρ̄ and level optimisation; the maximal ideal of T_{N(Σ)} lifting it with T_ℓ ∈ 𝔫 for ℓ ∈ Σ gives an isomorphism of localisations (EPW Proposition 2.6.2).

Reducedness and finite flatness over Λ: T′_{N(Σ)} ⊗_Λ L is a product of new Hecke algebras of levels dividing N(Σ) (EPW Proposition 2.4.2), and the ordinary Hecke algebra is finite flat over Λ (L0/ordinary-finite-over-lambda).
Branches: minimal primes of T_Σ correspond to local components of T_Σ ⊗_Λ L, each of which comes from a unique new level.
acceptance: T_Σ is reduced and finite flat over Λ, and its minimal primes correspond to Hida families of newforms with a definite tame conductor N(𝔞).

sources.locator: §2.6, Theorem 2.6.1, Proposition 2.6.2 and Definition 2.6.3, pp. 18–19; §2.7, Definition 2.7.1, Proposition 2.7.2 and Definition 2.7.3, pp. 19–20

nodes.title: Congruence modules of a branch of a Hida family
nodes.statement: For a branch 𝔞 of T_Σ (L1/reduced-hida-algebra), let λ_𝔞 : T_Σ → T(𝔞) be the quotient map. The family congruence module of an T_Σ-module M is Ψ_{λ_𝔞}(M) (L1/congruence-module, with O replaced by the local domain T(𝔞)) and the family congruence ideal is η_𝔞 = λ_𝔞(Ann_{T_Σ}(𝔞)) ⊆ T(𝔞). Since T_Σ is reduced and finite flat over Λ, Ψ_{λ_𝔞}(T_Σ) ≅ T(𝔞)/η_𝔞, a torsion T(𝔞)-module, and η_𝔞 = T(𝔞) iff Spec T(𝔞) meets no other branch. For the ordinary family symbol module M = M^±_𝔪 ⊗ T_Σ, free of rank one over T_Σ under the hypotheses of L1/family-symbol-free-rank-one, Ψ_{λ_𝔞}(M) ≅ T(𝔞)/η_𝔞 as well, and the choice of a trivialisation of M does not change it. For a primitive cuspidal component this is Hida's Λ-adic module of congruence: a finite torsion module over Λ with principal annihilator (Hida, Theorem 3.6), and for each k ≥ 2 the weight-k module of congruence between the forms belonging to the component and the other ordinary forms of weight k is the kernel of a canonical surjection between the weight-k fibres of Hida's two Λ-adic congruence modules (Hida, Corollary 3.8).
hypotheses: ρ̄ irreducible and p-distinguished (for freeness of M^±_𝔪); 𝔞 a minimal prime of T_Σ.
proofSteps: Reducedness of T_Σ gives Ann(Ann(𝔞)) = 𝔞, hence L1/congruence-ideal's identification.
Freeness of M^±_𝔪 (L1/family-symbol-free-rank-one) transports the computation from T_Σ to M; a different generator changes the isomorphism by a unit, not the module.
η_𝔞 = T(𝔞) iff Ann(𝔞) + 𝔞 = T_Σ iff the branch is a connected component of Spec T_Σ.
acceptance: Only the instance is planned here; the generic definition is L1/congruence-module.

sources.match: The branches of T_Σ and the freeness of the family symbol module that make the family congruence module well defined.

nodes.title: Change of trivialisation of the family period line
nodes.statement: Let θ^± : M^±_𝔪 ≅ T_𝔪 be a trivialisation of the invertible family symbol module (L1/family-period-line) and L_θ^± ∈ T_𝔪 ⊗̂ ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]] the scalar two-variable p-adic L-function obtained by applying θ^± to L^±(𝔪, N) (L1/family-measure). If θ′ = u·θ with u ∈ T_𝔪^×, then L_{θ′}^± = u·L_θ^±, and for every classical height-one prime ℘ the specialisations differ by the unit u(℘) ∈ O(℘)^×. Conversely, any two trivialisations differ by such a unit, so the ideal generated by L^±_θ in T_𝔪 ⊗̂ ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]] and the Iwasawa μ- and λ-invariants of its specialisations do not depend on θ; equality with single-form p-adic L-functions built from canonical periods holds up to a unit, never up to an arbitrary scalar in Frac O(℘).
hypotheses: ρ̄_𝔪 irreducible and p-distinguished, so that M^±_𝔪 is free of rank one.
proofSteps: θ′ ∘ θ⁻¹ is a T_𝔪-linear automorphism of T_𝔪, i.e. multiplication by a unit u.
Applying θ is T_𝔪-linear and commutes with the completed tensor product, so the formula follows; specialisation at ℘ is a ring map.
Comparison with canonical periods: at ℘ the specialised trivialisation is a generator of the saturated period lattice (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L1), which is unique up to O(℘)^×.
acceptance: The statement is integral: no p is inverted, and the ambiguity is a unit of T_𝔪, separating equality up to a unit from equality up to a field scalar as the stage requires.

sources.match: The L-functions L^±(𝔪, N) are defined up to a unit of T_𝔪 through the choice of generator, and their specialisations are p-adic L-functions with canonical periods up to units.

nodes.title: Two-variable p-adic L-functions on the branches of a Hida family
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ be as in L1/reduced-hida-algebra and 0 ≤ i ≤ p − 2, Λ^{(i)} the ω^i-component of ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]]. (1) L_Σ(ρ̄, ωⁱ) ∈ T_Σ ⊗̂ Λ^{(i)} is the image of L(𝔫, N(Σ), ωⁱ) (L1/family-measure) under T_Σ ≅ (T_{N(Σ)})_𝔫, defined up to T_Σ^×; its reductions modulo a height-one prime ℘ and modulo the maximal ideal are defined up to units. (2) For a branch 𝔞, L(ρ̄, 𝔞, ωⁱ) ∈ T(𝔞)° ⊗̂ Λ^{(i)} is the image of L(𝔪, N(𝔞), ωⁱ) under the surjection T_{N(𝔞)} → T^new_{N(𝔞)}/𝔞′ = T(𝔞)°; at a classical height-one prime ℘ of T(𝔞) it specialises to the p-adic L-function of the newform f_℘, whereas L_Σ(ρ̄, ωⁱ)(℘) is that of the Σ-imprimitive oldform g_℘. (3) Comparison: there is an isomorphism T(𝔞)° ⊗ M(N(Σ))_𝔫 ≅ T(𝔞)° ⊗ M(N(𝔞))_𝔪 compatible with complex conjugation carrying L(𝔫, N(Σ)) to L(𝔪, N(𝔞))·E_Σ(𝔞), with E_Σ(𝔞) = ∏_{ℓ∈Σ} E_ℓ(𝔞, ⟨ℓ⟩⁻¹) the product of Euler factors; hence L_Σ(ρ̄, ωⁱ) ≡ u·L(ρ̄, 𝔞, ωⁱ)·E_Σ(𝔞, ωⁱ) modulo 𝔞 for a unit u of T(𝔞)°.
hypotheses: ρ̄ irreducible, odd, ordinary, p-distinguished and modular, with a chosen p-stabilisation; Σ a finite set of primes ℓ ≠ p.
proofSteps: (1) and (2) are transports of L1/family-measure along the isomorphism of EPW Proposition 2.6.2 and the surjection (4.4); specialisation is L1/family-measure-specialisation.

(3) compares the family symbol modules of levels N(Σ) and N(𝔞) through degeneracy maps at the primes of Σ (EPW §4.5), the Euler factor arising from the U_ℓ-eigenvalue relations; the period ratio is shown to be a unit uniformly in the family.
acceptance: At every classical height-one prime ℘ of T(𝔞), L(ρ̄, 𝔞, ωⁱ) specialises to the p-adic L-function of the newform f_℘ up to a unit (EPW Proposition 4.1.4 with Definition 4.2.2).

nodes.title: Λ-adic forms as q-expansions and their duality with the ordinary Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 5, N = N₀p with p ∤ N₀, Λ = ℤ_p[[X]] with X ↔ γ − 1 for γ = 1 + p, and I a finite flat Λ-algebra. An ordinary Λ-adic cusp form of level N with coefficients in I is a formal q-expansion F = Σ_{n≥1} a(n, F)qⁿ ∈ I[[q]] such that for every arithmetic point P of I above P_k = (1 + X − (1 + p)^k) with k ≥ 2 the specialisation F mod P is the q-expansion of a classical ordinary cusp form of weight k and level N₀p (with the nebentypus determined by P). They form an I-module S^ord(N; I). The pairing (h, F) ↦ a(1, F|h) identifies S^ord(N; Λ) with Hom_Λ(h^ord(N; Λ), Λ), and normalised eigenforms in S^ord(N; I) correspond to Λ-algebra homomorphisms h^ord(N; Λ) → I. This definition does not use the Eisenstein family.
hypotheses: p ≥ 5; N₀ prime to p; specialisation required at every arithmetic point of weight k ≥ 2.
proofSteps: Weight-k duality: Hecke algebras and forms are dual under the first-coefficient pairing at every finite weight and level (L0/hecke-duality).

Freeness and control (L0/hida-control-theorem): h^ord(N; Λ) is free of finite rank and its fibre at P_k is the weight-k ordinary Hecke algebra; hence Hom_Λ(h^ord, Λ) specialises at every P_k to the dual of the weight-k Hecke algebra, i.e. to ordinary cusp forms of weight k, which is the q-expansion condition.

Conversely a family of q-expansions specialising to classical forms defines, through a(1, F|T(n)) = a(n, F), a Λ-linear functional on the Hecke algebra (the Hecke operators act on q-expansions coefficientwise and their action is determined at a Zariski-dense set of weights).
acceptance: Wiles's original definition (Invent. Math. 94, 1988) imposes the classicality condition only at a Zariski-dense set of weights; with Hida's control theorem the two versions agree, and this is the equivalence the stage asks for.

sources.locator: §2, Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 2.2, pp. 245–247; §3, (3.2), Theorem 3.1 and Corollary 3.2, pp. 249–250
sources.match: The duality between p-adic modular forms and Hecke algebras by the first-coefficient pairing, the continuous Λ-algebra structure of the Hecke algebras, freeness of the ordinary part and the control isomorphisms at every weight; together these give the q-expansion description of the dual of h^ord.

nodes.title: Primitive components of the ordinary Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: Let L be the fraction field of Λ_K and h^ord(N; 𝒪_K) the cuspidal ordinary Hecke algebra (p ≥ 5, N = N₀p). The algebra h^ord(N; K) := h^ord(N; 𝒪_K) ⊗_Λ L is a finite-dimensional L-algebra; its primitive part h^ord_prim (the part not coming from lower tame level) is semisimple, a product of finite field extensions 𝒦 of L (the primitive components). If 𝒦 is a primitive cuspidal component with d = [𝒦 : L], then for every k ≥ 2 exactly d ordinary eigenforms of weight k and level Γ₁(N₀p) belong to 𝒦, their associated newforms have conductor divisible by N₀, and conversely every ordinary eigenform of weight k ≥ 2 whose newform has conductor divisible by N₀ belongs to a unique primitive component. The algebraic closure of ℚ_p in 𝒦 is a finite extension of K, and primitive components are compatible with extension of K.
hypotheses: p ≥ 5; N₀ prime to p; cuspidal components.
proofSteps: Semisimplicity: the primitive part of h^ord ⊗ L injects into a product over classical weights of semisimple new Hecke algebras (Hecke operators on newforms are semisimple), so it has no nilradical.

Counting: the image of h^ord in 𝒦 is finite over Λ of generic rank d, and by control (L0/hida-control-theorem) its fibre at P_k embeds in the weight-k Hecke algebra; each homomorphism to ℚ̄_p is an eigenform, giving exactly d of them for k ≥ 2.
Prop 3.4: Λ_K ⊆ 𝒦 and X is transcendental over the algebraic closure M of ℚ_p in 𝒦, so [M : K] divides [𝒦 : L].
acceptance: The non-primitive part of h^ord ⊗ L need not be semisimple (oldforms with repeated U_ℓ-eigenvalues), which is why the statement is for primitive components; L1/reduced-hida-algebra removes the U_ℓ to obtain a reduced algebra.

sources.locator: §3, Proposition 3.4, Theorem 3.5 and the terminology before them, pp. 251–252; Theorem 3.6 and Corollary 3.7, p. 253
sources.match: Primitive components of the ordinary Hecke algebra over the fraction field of Λ_K, their fields of definition, and the exact count of ordinary forms of each weight k ≥ 2 belonging to a primitive cuspidal component.

nodes.title: Nakayama's lemma for compact modules over complete local rings
nodes.statement: Let Λ be a complete noetherian local ring with maximal ideal 𝔪 and finite residue field, and M a compact Hausdorff topological Λ-module (equivalently a profinite Λ-module; for example the Pontryagin dual of a discrete Λ-module). Then ⋂_n 𝔪ⁿM = 0 and M = lim_n M/𝔪ⁿM; if M/𝔪M is finite, then M is finitely generated over Λ, and any lifts of generators of M/𝔪M generate M.
hypotheses: Λ complete noetherian local with finite residue field; M compact Hausdorff.
proofSteps: M is the limit of its finite discrete quotients M/U; each is a finite Λ-module, hence killed by some 𝔪ⁿ, so 𝔪ⁿM ⊆ U and ⋂ 𝔪ⁿM = 0.
Let N be the submodule generated by lifts x_1, …, x_r of generators of M/𝔪M; it is the image of the continuous map Λ^r → M, hence compact and closed.
By induction M = N + 𝔪ⁿM for all n, and N = ⋂_n (N + 𝔪ⁿM) because N is closed and the 𝔪ⁿM form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0.
acceptance: This replaces the earlier citation of NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa NE.0, a roadmap outside the upstream order; the lemma moves down here.

sources.match: Finiteness of the ordinary Hecke algebra over Λ is deduced from finiteness modulo the maximal ideal by Nakayama's lemma for compact Λ-modules.

nodes.title: Hida's ordinary projector on definite quaternionic forms
nodes.statement: F is a totally real field of even degree d, p an odd prime, D/F the quaternion algebra ramified exactly at the infinite places, X(U) = D^×\G^D(A_f)/U for open compact U ⊆ GL₂(𝒪_F ⊗ Ẑ) with U_v = GL₂(𝒪_{F,v}) for v | p, U_a = U ∩ U(p^a) and U⁰_a = U ∩ U₀(p^a), and 𝒪 the ring of integers of a finite extension K of ℚ_p. For an 𝒪-module R, H⁰(X(U_a), R) is the module of R-valued functions on the finite set X(U_a), with the Hecke operators T₀(p) = [U_a (1 0; 0 ϖ_p) U_a] (ϖ_p a finite idele with a uniformiser at each v | p and 1 elsewhere), T₀(𝔭_i) for the primes above p, the group G(U_a) and T(ℓ), S(ℓ) for ℓ ∤ p with U_ℓ maximal. For R finite as a set, e := lim_n T₀(p)^{n!} is the finite ordinary projector of L0a; for R = 𝒪 it is the adic projector on the finite free module H⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪); for R = K/𝒪 it is the colimit of the projectors on the 𝒪/πⁿ-coefficients. e is an idempotent commuting with the Hecke algebra T(U_a, 𝒪), with change of coefficients R → R′, and with pullback and trace between levels U_b ⊆ U_a.
hypotheses: F even degree, p odd, D definite and unramified at all finite places.
proofSteps: H⁰(X(U_a), R) = Map(X(U_a), R) is finite (resp. finite free) because X(U_a) is finite (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.3, the definite class set).
Apply L0a/finite-ordinary-projector and L0a/adic-instance; the projector for K/𝒪 is the colimit by naturality (L0a/ordinary-projector-natural).

Commutation with the Hecke algebra and with the level maps: these are 𝒪-linear and commute with T₀(p) (Skinner–Wiles's computation of double cosets), so they commute with every power and with the limit.
acceptance: Moved down from OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.1 (tier 20) to this tier-16 layer, as the upstream order requires; R21.1 imports it from here.

nodes.title: The nearly ordinary Hecke algebra T_∞(U, 𝒪)
nodes.statement: F is a totally real field of even degree d, p an odd prime, D/F the quaternion algebra ramified exactly at the infinite places, X(U) = D^×\G^D(A_f)/U for open compact U ⊆ GL₂(𝒪_F ⊗ Ẑ) with U_v = GL₂(𝒪_{F,v}) for v | p, U_a = U ∩ U(p^a) and U⁰_a = U ∩ U₀(p^a), and 𝒪 the ring of integers of a finite extension K of ℚ_p. Let T(U_a, 𝒪) ⊆ End_𝒪(H⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪)) be generated by T₀(p), the T₀(𝔭_i), G(U_a) and T(ℓ), S(ℓ) for ℓ ∤ p with U_ℓ maximal, and T₂(U_a, 𝒪) := eT(U_a, 𝒪), its image in End_𝒪(eH⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪)). The transition maps T₂(U_b, 𝒪) → T₂(U_a, 𝒪) (b ≥ a) are surjective and T_∞(U, 𝒪) := lim_a T₂(U_a, 𝒪). With G(U) = lim_a G(U_a) ≅ (𝒪_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× × Z(U) there is a continuous map 𝒪[[G(U)]] → T_∞(U, 𝒪), making T_∞(U, 𝒪) an algebra over the weight algebra Λ′_𝒪 of L5/totally-real-weight-algebra.
hypotheses: As in L5/quaternionic-ordinary-projector.
proofSteps: The transition maps are restrictions of Hecke operators along the pullback maps, which are compatible with e; surjectivity holds because generators map to generators.
The G(U_a) act through the diamond-type operators, compatible in a, giving 𝒪[[G(U)]] → T_∞(U, 𝒪) by the universal property of the completed group ring (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1).

By the Jacquet–Langlands correspondence for definite quaternion algebras (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.3), T₂(U_a, 𝒪) is Skinner–Wiles's Hecke algebra eT*₂(U_a, 𝒪) of Hilbert cusp forms of parallel weight two.
acceptance: Moved down from OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.1.

nodes.title: The ordinary part does not grow in Γ₀(p^a)-level
nodes.statement: F is a totally real field of even degree d, p an odd prime, D/F the quaternion algebra ramified exactly at the infinite places, X(U) = D^×\G^D(A_f)/U for open compact U ⊆ GL₂(𝒪_F ⊗ Ẑ) with U_v = GL₂(𝒪_{F,v}) for v | p, U_a = U ∩ U(p^a) and U⁰_a = U ∩ U₀(p^a), and 𝒪 the ring of integers of a finite extension K of ℚ_p. For a ≥ 2 the double coset U⁰_a (1 0; 0 ϖ_p) U⁰_a equals U⁰_a (1 0; 0 ϖ_p) U⁰_{a−1}, so T₀(p) maps H⁰(X(U⁰_a), K/𝒪) into the image of H⁰(X(U⁰_{a−1}), K/𝒪), and eH⁰(X(U⁰_a), K/𝒪) = eH⁰(X(U⁰_1), K/𝒪). Moreover H⁰(X(U⁰_a), K/𝒪) = H⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪)^{G(U_a)}.
hypotheses: As in L5/quaternionic-ordinary-projector.
proofSteps: The double coset identity is a matrix computation at the places above p.

Iterating, the image of T₀(p)^{a−1} lies in the level-U⁰_1 forms, and e is a limit of powers of T₀(p) on which T₀(p) is invertible, so the ordinary part is contained in, hence equal to, the level-U⁰_1 ordinary part.
Invariants: U⁰_a/U_a ≅ G(U_a)-part acting on X(U_a).
acceptance: Moved down from OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.1.

sources.locator: §3.2, proof of Proposition 3.3, p. 36 (Numdam PDF page 33)
sources.match: The double coset identity and the resulting independence of the ordinary part from the Γ₀(p^a)-level, and the identification of U⁰_a-invariants with G(U_a)-invariants.

nodes.title: Pontryagin duality for the ordinary quaternionic towers
nodes.statement: F is a totally real field of even degree d, p an odd prime, D/F the quaternion algebra ramified exactly at the infinite places, X(U) = D^×\G^D(A_f)/U for open compact U ⊆ GL₂(𝒪_F ⊗ Ẑ) with U_v = GL₂(𝒪_{F,v}) for v | p, U_a = U ∩ U(p^a) and U⁰_a = U ∩ U₀(p^a), and 𝒪 the ring of integers of a finite extension K of ℚ_p. Put H_∞(U) = lim_→ eH⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪) and H⁺_∞(U) = lim_→ eH⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪)⁺ along pullbacks, and M_∞(U) = lim_← eH⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪)⁺, M⁺_∞(U) = lim_← eH⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪) along traces (the superscript + denoting the subspace on which the centre acts through the norm-form condition fixed by Skinner–Wiles). These are T_∞(U, 𝒪)-modules, and the perfect pairings at finite level induce T_∞(U, 𝒪)-isomorphisms M_∞(U) ≅ Hom_𝒪(H_∞(U), K/𝒪) and M⁺_∞(U) ≅ Hom_𝒪(H⁺_∞(U), K/𝒪).
hypotheses: As in L5/quaternionic-ordinary-projector.
proofSteps: The pairing on functions on X(U_a) weighted by the stabiliser orders c_{U_a}(x) is perfect over 𝒪 when the stabilisers are trivial, which holds for a large (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.3, integral pairing and neat level).

Hecke operators are adjoint up to the twist by the main involution; e is compatible with the pairing, and pullback is adjoint to trace, so the finite-level dualities pass to the limit (Pontryagin duality exchanges colimits and limits).
acceptance: Moved down from OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.1.

sources.match: The ordinary towers H_∞, M_∞ and their ± variants, the stabiliser-weighted pairings and the Pontryagin duality between the towers.

nodes.title: Λ-adic Hilbert modular forms and their ordinary parts
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real, p odd, E/ℚ_p finite with ring of integers 𝒪_E, Λ = 𝒪_E[[T]], u a topological generator of 1 + pℤ_p and ν_k : Λ → 𝒪_E, T ↦ u^{k−1} − 1, the weight-k specialisation. For a narrow ray class character χ of conductor 𝔫 prime to p, a Λ-adic Hilbert modular form of tame level 𝔫 and character χ is a family F = (c(𝔞, F))_𝔞 ∈ Λ^{integral ideals} together with constant terms, such that for every integer k ≥ 2 the specialisation ν_k(F) is the q-expansion of a classical Hilbert modular form of parallel weight k, level 𝔫p and character χω^{1−k}. They form a Λ-module M(𝔫, χ) with cuspidal submodule S(𝔫, χ), Hecke operators T_𝔩 (𝔩 ∤ 𝔫p) and U_𝔩 (𝔩 | 𝔫p). The ordinary projector e = lim_n (∏_{𝔭|p} U_𝔭)^{n!} defines the Hida families M°(𝔫, χ) = eM(𝔫, χ) and S°(𝔫, χ) = eS(𝔫, χ), finite free over Λ, with Hecke algebras T̃ and T acting on them.
hypotheses: F totally real; p odd; χ of conductor 𝔫 prime to p; parallel weights.
proofSteps: The ordinary projector is L0a's: on each specialisation the space of forms of level 𝔫p^r and weight k is a finite 𝒪_E-module on which ∏U_𝔭 acts, and the projectors are compatible; Hida's theory identifies eM(𝔫, χ) with a finite free Λ-module whose specialisations at k ≥ 2 are the ordinary classical forms (Hida control in parallel weight, L5/hida-control-nearly-ordinary for the cuspidal part).

The q-expansion principle for p-adic Hilbert modular forms on the ordinary Igusa tower makes 'a family of q-expansions specialising to classical forms' a module of p-adic modular forms (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T5, as red-team finding RT-AREA-langlands-1/8 requires, not IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.1).
acceptance: Weight-one specialisation ν_1 is not required to be classical in the definition; Dasgupta–Kakde–Ventullo study it separately.

sources.locator: §3.1, (25)–(27) and the definitions of M(𝔫, χ), S(𝔫, χ), e, M°, S°, T̃, T, pp. 846–847

nodes.title: A Hida family is determined by its Fourier expansion
nodes.statement: Let Λ_{(1)} = 𝒪_E[[T]]_{(T)} be the localisation of Λ at the weight-one prime (T) (a discrete valuation ring in which p is invertible). The map c : S°(𝔫, χ)_{(1)} → ∏_{𝔞 ⊆ 𝒪_F} Λ_{(1)}, H ↦ (c(𝔞, H))_𝔞, sending a cuspidal Hida family to its normalised Fourier coefficients, is injective and Λ_{(1)}-linear.
hypotheses: χ of conductor 𝔫 prime to p; cuspidal families.
proofSteps: A Λ-adic form is by definition a family of coefficients; the Fourier expansion map is injective on S(𝔫, χ) because a cuspidal Hilbert form is determined by its normalised coefficients c(𝔞, ·) (its constant terms vanish), so a family all of whose coefficients vanish specialises to zero at every k ≥ 2, hence is zero.
Localisation at (T) is flat, so injectivity persists after ⊗_Λ Λ_{(1)}.
acceptance: The paper uses this without proof; it is one of the three facts the maintainer assigned to this layer.

sources.match: A Hida family is determined by its Fourier expansion: the canonical injective Λ_{(1)}-linear map from S°(𝔫, χ)_{(1)} to the product of copies of Λ_{(1)} indexed by integral ideals.

nodes.title: The localised cuspidal Hecke algebra is reduced at minimal tame level
nodes.statement: Let 𝔪 ⊆ T be the height-one prime of the cuspidal Hecke algebra generated by T, T_𝔩 − (1 + χε(𝔩)) for 𝔩 ∤ 𝔫p and U_𝔩 − 1 for 𝔩 | 𝔫p (the Eisenstein prime through E₁(1, χ_S)). If the tame character χ has conductor equal to the tame level 𝔫, then the localisation T_{(𝔪)} is reduced: there are no 𝔫-old forms, so T_{(𝔪)} ⊗ Frac(Λ) is a product of fields.
hypotheses: cond(χ) = 𝔫; the localisation at the height-one prime 𝔪.
proofSteps: At tame level equal to the conductor of the character every eigenform is new at 𝔫, and the U_𝔩 (𝔩 | 𝔫) act semisimply with eigenvalues determined by the newform; away from 𝔫p the T_𝔩 act semisimply on cusp forms (they are normal for the Petersson product at each classical weight).

S°(𝔫, χ) ⊗ Frac(Λ) is therefore a direct sum of one-dimensional Hecke eigenspaces (multiplicity one for new families), so the Hecke algebra over Frac(Λ) is a product of fields and T_{(𝔪)}, being Λ_{(1)}-torsion-free and embedded in it, is reduced.
acceptance: The hypothesis cond(χ) = 𝔫 is essential: with old forms at a prime 𝔩 | 𝔫, U_𝔩 has repeated eigenvalues on oldspaces and the Hecke algebra including U_𝔩 can contain nilpotents.

sources.match: Since the conductor of χ equals the tame level there are no 𝔫-old forms, so T_{(𝔪)} is reduced; the paper credits the observation to Hida and refers to Hida's proof of Theorem 3.6 and Corollary 3.7.

nodes.title: The total ring of fractions of the localised Hecke algebra and its eigenfamilies
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of L5/hilbert-hecke-reduced, let L = Frac(T_{(𝔪)}) be the total ring of fractions. Then T_{(𝔪)} ↪ L and L ≅ ∏_{i=1}^t L_{H_i}, a finite product of fields, each a finite extension of Frac(Λ) corresponding to a cuspidal Hida eigenfamily H_i; the image of T_𝔞 in L_{H_i} is the normalised coefficient c(𝔞, H_i). These coefficients generate a finite local Λ-subalgebra Λ_{H_i} ⊆ L_{H_i}, the image of T_{(𝔪)} in L_{H_i} is the localisation of Λ_{H_i} at a height-one prime 𝔪_{H_i} over (T), and c(𝔩, H_i) ≡ 1 + χ(𝔩) mod 𝔪_{H_i} for 𝔩 ∤ 𝔫p and c(𝔩, H_i) ≡ 1 mod 𝔪_{H_i} for 𝔩 | 𝔫p: each H_i specialises at 𝔪_{H_i} to the weight-one form E₁(1, χ_S).
hypotheses: As in L5/hilbert-hecke-reduced.
proofSteps: A reduced noetherian ring of dimension one localised at a height-one prime embeds in the product of its residue fields at minimal primes (Mathlib: reduced rings embed in the product over minimal primes).

The minimal primes of T_{(𝔪)} correspond to the Hecke eigensystems in S°(𝔫, χ) ⊗ Frac(Λ)ᵃˡᵍ that specialise into 𝔪, i.e. to cuspidal Hida eigenfamilies; the field of each is generated over Frac(Λ) by its coefficients.
The congruences are the description of 𝔪 by its generators.
acceptance: Each eigenfamily H_i specialises at 𝔪_{H_i} to E₁(1, χ_S), as the congruences (51) state.

nodes.title: Hida's big Galois representation and its nearly ordinary twist
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 3, Γ = Gal(ℚ_∞/ℚ) for the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension and Γ′ the diamond group of the tower Y₁(p^t), both identified with 1 + pℤ_p. For a branch of the ordinary Hecke algebra with coefficient ring H^ord_F (a local domain finite flat over ℤ_p[[Γ′]], attached to a Λ-adic eigen newform F), there is a finitely generated torsion-free H^ord_F-module T^ord of generic rank two with a continuous G_ℚ-action, unramified outside a finite set S ∋ p, ∞, with trace(Frob_ℓ) = T_ℓ for ℓ ∉ S. The nearly ordinary Hecke algebra is H^{n.o.}_F := H^ord_F ⊗̂_{ℤ_p} ℤ_p[[Γ]] ≅ H^ord_F[[Γ]], and the nearly ordinary deformation is T := T^ord ⊗̂ ℤ_p[[Γ]](χ̃) ⊗ ωⁱ, with χ̃ : G_ℚ ↠ Γ ⊂ ℤ_p[[Γ]]^× the universal cyclotomic character. Under the hypothesis (F) that T is free of rank two over H^{n.o.}_F with irreducible residual representation: det T is χ̃²χ̃′^{−1} times the inverse cyclotomic character up to finite order, and for an arithmetic point κ of weight w(κ) and 1 ≤ j ≤ w(κ) + 1 the specialisation of T along χ^{j−1} ∘ κ is the twist T_{f_κ} ⊗ χ^j of Deligne's lattice of the normalised eigenform f_κ of weight w(κ) + 2.
hypotheses: p ≥ 3; a branch H^ord_F of the ordinary Hecke algebra; hypothesis (F) for the freeness statements.
proofSteps: The ordinary parts of the p-adic Tate modules of J₁(Np^t) (ModularCurvesPartII R14.2) form a projective system of H^ord-modules with Galois action; their limit, localised at the branch, is T^ord (Hida's construction; equivalently, the Galois action on the family symbol module of L1 through the comparison of étale and Betti homology).

The trace and determinant identities hold at the Zariski-dense set of weight-two points by the Eichler–Shimura relation (ModularCurvesPartII R14.6) and extend by continuity; equivalently, the trace determinant is obtained by interpolating the determinants of the classical points through finite quotients (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.4).

Specialisation at an arithmetic point of weight w(κ) + 2 is Deligne's representation by Hida's control theorem (L0/hida-control-theorem) and the Eichler–Shimura comparison at weight w(κ) + 2 through L1's family symbols.
acceptance: This is the rational (F = ℚ) ordinary big Galois representation; RS-08 named OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.3 as owner, but R21.3 is in tier 20 and plans the totally real nearly ordinary representation of Skinner–Wiles; the rational construction moves down here, and R21.3 imports it for F = ℚ.

nodes.title: The ordinary filtration of the big Galois representation at p
nodes.statement: Under (F), the restriction of T to a decomposition group G_{ℚ_p} has a filtration 0 → F⁺T → T → F⁻T → 0 by H^{n.o.}_F-submodules free of rank one, with F⁺T ≅ ℤ_p[[Γ]](χ̃) ⊗̂ H^ord_F(α̃) ⊗ ωⁱ where α̃ : G_{ℚ_p} → (H^ord_F)^× is unramified with α̃(Frob_p) = A_p and κ(A_p) = a_p(f_κ) at every arithmetic point; F⁻T is unramified up to the twist by the inverse of the determinant character. The filtration specialises at every arithmetic point to the ordinary filtration of T_{f_κ} ⊗ χ^j, and is saturated (the quotient F⁻T is torsion-free).
hypotheses: Hypothesis (F); p-distinguished residual representation for uniqueness of the filtration.
proofSteps: At weight-two points of level Np^t the ordinary part of the Tate module has a connected–étale filtration from the ordinary reduction of the ordinary part of J₁(Np^t) at p (Mazur–Wiles), with unramified quotient on which Frob_p acts by U_p; pass to the limit.
The sub and quotient are rank one by (F) and residual p-distinguishedness, and the unramified character α̃ interpolates U_p.
Specialisation compatibility follows from the uniqueness of the ordinary filtration of a p-distinguished representation.
acceptance: The ordinarity at p of the weight-two Jacobian (Mazur–Wiles) is requested from ModularCurvesPartII R14.6 with the semistable Tate interface; this layer adds only the passage to the limit.

sources.match: The G_{ℚ_p}-stable filtration with graded pieces free of rank one over H^{n.o.}_F, and the description of F⁺T through the cyclotomic character and the unramified character α̃ interpolating a_p.
The ordinary shape of the restriction to a decomposition group at p of the representation attached to a maximal ideal of the ordinary Hecke algebra.

nodes.title: Greenberg and Bloch–Kato Selmer groups of the nearly ordinary deformation
nodes.statement: Let A = T ⊗_{H^{n.o.}} Hom_{ℤ_p}(H^{n.o.}_F, ℚ_p/ℤ_p) be the discrete module attached to T and ℚ_S the maximal extension unramified outside S. For a local condition H¹_?(ℚ_p, A) ⊆ H¹(ℚ_p, A), Sel_?(T) is the kernel of H¹(ℚ_S/ℚ, A) → ∏_{ℓ∈S, ℓ≠p} H¹(ℚ_ℓ, A)/H¹_ur(ℚ_ℓ, A) × H¹(ℚ_p, A)/H¹_?(ℚ_p, A). Greenberg's condition is H¹_Gr = ker(H¹(ℚ_p, A) → H¹(ℚ_p^ur, F⁻A)); the Bloch–Kato condition is the limit of the Bloch–Kato finite parts H¹_f on the Φ_{s,t}^{(j,k)}-torsion of A along the height-two ideals of arithmetic points. Under (F): Sel_BK(T) = Sel_Gr(T), independent of (j, k), and its Pontryagin dual is a finitely generated torsion H^{n.o.}_F-module.
hypotheses: Hypothesis (F).
proofSteps: The Greenberg condition is SelmerIwasawaCohomology L2's Greenberg local condition for the filtration of L4/ordinary-filtration; Selmer groups and their duals are L2's constructions over the coefficient ring H^{n.o.}_F.

Equality of the two Selmer groups: at each arithmetic specialisation the ordinary Greenberg condition agrees with the Bloch–Kato finite condition up to finite error controlled uniformly (Ochiai, A generalization of the Coleman map, §4); pass to the limit.
Torsionness: specialise to a weight and use Kato's cyclotomic theorem (KatoEulerSystems L4) and the control theorem for Selmer groups (SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3).
acceptance: Under (F) the dual Selmer group is torsion, which is what makes a characteristic ideal and a main conjecture meaningful.

sources.match: The discrete module A, Selmer groups for a chosen local condition at p, Greenberg's and the Bloch–Kato conditions, and Proposition A: the two agree and their duals are torsion, citing Ochiai's earlier work for the equality and Kato and Rubin for torsionness.

nodes.title: The Selmer complex of the nearly ordinary deformation
nodes.statement: With Greenberg's local condition F⁺T → T at p and unramified conditions at ℓ ∈ S ∖ {p}, Nekovář's Selmer complex RΓ_f(ℚ, T) is a perfect complex of H^{n.o.}_F-modules with H¹ the compact Selmer group and H² a module whose Pontryagin dual is related to Sel(T) up to local error terms; it satisfies derived control: RΓ_f(ℚ, T) ⊗^L_{H^{n.o.}} H^{n.o.}/𝔓 ≅ RΓ_f(ℚ, T ⊗ H^{n.o.}/𝔓) for every height-two arithmetic prime 𝔓, and its determinant gives the characteristic ideal of the Selmer group.
hypotheses: Hypothesis (F); Greenberg conditions.
proofSteps: Instance of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3's Iwasawa Selmer complex with coefficients the complete local ring H^{n.o.}_F, using the local filtration of L4/ordinary-filtration.

Derived control is SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3's derived specialisation with the local correction complexes, which vanish for Greenberg conditions because F⁺T is a direct summand of T as H^{n.o.}-module.
acceptance: The stage asks for the family Selmer complex 'through R07', now SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3; only the instance is planned here.

nodes.title: Beilinson–Kato classes in Hida families
nodes.statement: Under (F), let R be the set of square-free integers prime to S. There is a family Z(r) ∈ H¹(ℚ(ζ_r), T*(1)), r ∈ R, unramified outside the primes above S, with the Euler system norm relations Norm_{ℚ(ζ_{rq})/ℚ(ζ_r)} Z(rq) = P_q(Frob_q) Z(r) for primes q ∤ r, where P_q(X) = det(1 − Frob_q X | T) ∈ H^{n.o.}_F[X] and Frob_q is a geometric Frobenius. For every arithmetic point κ and 1 ≤ j ≤ w(κ) + 1, the specialisation z_{(j,κ)}(1) of Z(1) is Kato's zeta element for f_κ twisted by χ^j, and the dual exponential of its image in H¹_{/f}(ℚ_p, T_{(j,κ)}*(1)) equals L^{(p)}(f*_κ, ω^{i−j}, j)/((2π√−1)^{j−1} C^{(−1)^i}_{∞,κ}) · δ^{dR}_κ, with L^{(p)} the L-function without its Euler factor at p and C^±_{∞,κ} complex periods.
hypotheses: Hypothesis (F); p ≥ 3.
proofSteps: At each level Np^t and each cyclotomic level, Kato's zeta elements of KatoEulerSystems L2 lie in the étale cohomology of the modular curves; their ordinary projections are compatible under the trace maps in the weight (via the moment maps, KatoEulerSystems L1) and in the cyclotomic variable (KatoEulerSystems L2 norm relations).
The limit over both towers defines Z(r) in Iwasawa cohomology of T*(1); the norm relations are inherited.
The dual-exponential formula at arithmetic points is Kato's explicit reciprocity law (KatoEulerSystems L3) at the specialised form.
acceptance: At every arithmetic point the dual exponential of the specialised class is the critical L-value over the complex period (Proposition 1.2(3)).

sources.locator: §1, Proposition 1.2 with the de Rham conventions before it, pp. 117–118
sources.match: The Beilinson–Kato elements Z(r) for the nearly ordinary deformation, their norm relations with the Euler factors P_q, and the interpolation of Kato's dual exponential formula at every arithmetic point.

nodes.title: The Perrin-Riou big logarithm in families
nodes.statement: Let M be an unramified profinite ℤ_p[G_{ℚ_p}]-module (for example the unramified twist of F⁻T*(1) attached to a Hida family) and D(M) = (M ⊗̂ ℤ_p^{ur})^{G_{ℚ_p}} with Frobenius φ. There is a map L_M : H¹(ℚ_p, M ⊗̂ Λ_Γ(−j)) → D(M) ⊗̂ I^{−1}Λ_Γ, where I is the kernel of specialisation at j = −1, functorial in M and commuting with End_{ℤ_p[G_{ℚ_p}]}(M), with kernel H⁰(ℚ_p, M) and image of the reduction modulo I contained in D(M)^{φ=1}; for M finite free over ℤ_p it is Perrin-Riou's big logarithm. Composed with the projection to the unramified quotient F⁻ of the local cohomology of T*(1), it gives the family Coleman map Ξ : H¹_{/f}(ℚ_p, T*(1)) → H^{n.o.}_F of Ochiai.
hypotheses: M unramified and profinite; Hida-family coefficients for the application.
proofSteps: Define N(M) = D(M)[[π]] with φ and its left inverse ψ, use Fontaine's isomorphism H¹(ℚ_p, M ⊗ Λ_Γ(−j)) ≅ (π⁻¹N(M))^{ψ=1} and the exact sequence for 1 − φ; φ is invertible on D(M), so N(M)^{ψ=0} = D(M) ⊗̂ Λ_Γ.
Both sides commute with inverse limits, so the case of finite M suffices.
acceptance: Ochiai's own construction of Ξ (Amer. J. Math. 125, 2003) is not freely available; the family regulator is planned through KLZ's big logarithm, which applies to F⁻T*(1) because it is unramified up to a twist by the cyclotomic variable.

sources.locator: §8.2, Definition 8.2.1 and Theorem 8.2.3 with proof, p. 42 (arXiv v6)
sources.match: The module D(M) of an unramified profinite module, the big logarithm L_M with its functoriality, kernel and image, built from the module D(M)[[π]] and Fontaine's isomorphism.
Ochiai's map Ξ from H¹_{/f}(ℚ_p, T*(1)) to H^{n.o.}_F, constructed in his 2003 paper, whose image of the local Beilinson–Kato class is the two-variable p-adic L-function.
