nodes.title: The two-variable p-adic L-function of a Hida family and the family reciprocity law
nodes.statement: Under (F), set L_p(T) := Ξ(loc_{/f}(Z(1))) ∈ H^{n.o.}_F (in Frac H^{n.o.}_F, integral when H^{n.o.}_F is integrally closed). Then (1) for every height-one prime 𝔭 of H^{n.o.}_F, length_{(H^{n.o.})_𝔭} (H¹_{/f}(ℚ_p, T*(1))/loc_{/f}(Z(1)))_𝔭 = ord_𝔭(L_p(T)); (2) for every arithmetic (j, κ) with 0 ≤ j − 1 ≤ w(κ), (χ^{j−1} ∘ κ)(L_p(T))/C_{p,κ} equals (−1)^{j−1}(j − 1)!·(1 − ω^{i−j}(p)p^{j−1}/a_p(f_κ))·(p^{j−1}/a_p(f_κ))^{q(i,j)}·G(ω^{j−i})·L(f_κ, ω^{i−j}, j)/((2π√−1)^{j−1}C^{(−1)^i}_{∞,κ}), with C_{p,κ} a p-adic period, G a Gauss sum and q(i, j) the p-order of the conductor of ω^{i−j}. The interpolation is derived from Kato's reciprocity law at each arithmetic point, not imposed as a definition, and on a branch L_p(T) agrees with the Mazur–Kitagawa two-variable L-function of L1 up to a unit of the branch times the ratio of p-adic and complex periods.
hypotheses: Hypothesis (F); H^{n.o.}_F integrally closed for integrality.
proofSteps: (2): specialise Ξ at (j, κ), where it becomes the Bloch–Kato dual exponential with the Euler-like factor (L4/family-big-logarithm), and apply the dual-exponential formula of L4/big-beilinson-kato-classes.

(1): the map Ξ is injective with pseudo-null cokernel on the rank-one module H¹_{/f}(ℚ_p, T*(1)) (local Euler characteristic and F⁻ unramified), so lengths at height-one primes are computed by ord_𝔭 of the image.

Comparison with L1: both interpolate the same critical values at a Zariski-dense set of arithmetic points up to periods; on a branch, the ratio is a unit times the period ratio (L1/period-change-of-trivialisation).
acceptance: The family reciprocity law is derived from the single-form reciprocity laws and the construction of Ξ, as the stage requires; it is not a definition of the family class.

sources.match: The two-variable p-adic L-function as the image of the local Beilinson–Kato class under Ξ, the length formula at height-one primes, the interpolation formula at arithmetic points, and the integrality caveat when H^{n.o.} is not normal.

nodes.title: Euler system divisibility for the nearly ordinary deformation
nodes.statement: Assume (F), that H^{n.o.}_F ≅ 𝒪[[X₁, X₂]] for the ring of integers 𝒪 of a finite extension of ℚ_p, and that there are τ ∈ G_{ℚ(μ_{p^∞})} acting on T by a unipotent matrix (1 P_τ; 0 1) with P_τ ≠ 0 and τ′ ∈ G_ℚ acting by −1. Then there is k ≥ 0 such that for every height-one prime 𝔭 of H^{n.o.}_F, length (Sel(T)^∨)_𝔭 ≤ length (H¹_{/f}(ℚ_p, T*(1))/loc_{/f}(Z(1)))_𝔭 + ord_𝔭(P_τ^k). Combined with L4/two-variable-l-function, char(Sel(T)^∨) divides L_p(T)·P_τ^k: one divisibility of Greenberg's two-variable main conjecture for Hida families, up to the factor P_τ^k.
hypotheses: (F); H^{n.o.}_F a two-variable power series ring; the elements τ, τ′ as stated.
proofSteps: Ochiai's Euler system argument over the deformation ring: Kolyvagin derivative classes are built from Z(r) and controlled at height-two specialisations, where Kato–Rubin's cyclotomic bound applies; the bounds at a Zariski-dense set of height-two primes assemble to a bound at each height-one prime, the defect measured by P_τ.
The identification of the right-hand side with ord_𝔭 L_p(T) is L4/two-variable-l-function (1).
acceptance: The hypotheses are visible: when H^{n.o.} is not regular, or no τ with nonzero P_τ exists, no bound is asserted.

sources.locator: §1, Theorem C and the final Theorem, pp. 120–121; §2, Theorems 2.4 and 2.6
sources.match: The Euler system bound for Galois deformations over a two-variable power series ring under the existence of τ and τ′, and the resulting inequality towards the two-variable main conjecture.

nodes.title: Triangulations and the regulator over Coleman families
nodes.statement: Let f_α be a noble refined eigenform (p-regular and non-critical slope) of weight k + 2 and F the Coleman family through it over an affinoid disc V of weight space (PadicFamilies L2), with Galois representation M_V(F)* over O(V). After shrinking V: (1) the (φ, Γ)-module D†_rig(M_V(F)*) over the Robba ring over O(V) admits a canonical triangulation 0 → F⁺D → D → F⁻D → 0 with F⁻D ≅ R_{O(V)}(α_F⁻¹) and F⁺D a rank-one module given by α_F·ε_F(p)⁻¹ twisted by 1 + κ_V; (2) there is an O(V)-basis vector ω_F of (F⁻D(1 + κ_V + ε(p)_F))^{Γ=1} specialising at each classical weight t to the differential of f_t (Eichler–Shimura in families); (3) the Perrin-Riou regulator of the rank-one quotient is defined over O(V) ⊗̂ O(𝒲) and specialises at classical points to Bloch–Kato logarithms or dual exponentials with explicit Euler factors. No constant-dimension crystalline module over the whole eigencurve neighbourhood is asserted: the triangulation exists only after shrinking around a noble point.
hypotheses: f_α noble; V a sufficiently small affinoid disc around its weight.
proofSteps: Liu's triangulation theorem for families of refined trianguline representations gives (1) at a non-critical point, after shrinking V.
(2) is Andreatta–Iovita–Stevens's overconvergent Eichler–Shimura comparison composed with projection to F⁻ (Sen theory in families).
(3) is the regulator for rank-one (φ, Γ)-modules over Robba rings over affinoids (Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao), applied to F⁻ and paired with ω_F.
acceptance: The theorem is source-scoped as RS-08 requires: it covers Coleman families through noble points, with the triangulation hypothesis visible; the construction of Galois representations over the eigencurve and Liu's and Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao's theorems are imported as recorded inputs (gap 'Nonordinary family inputs').

nodes.title: Period modules of totally real Hida families
nodes.statement: In the setting of L5/ordinary-towers-duality, let 𝔪 be a maximal ideal of T_∞(U, 𝒪) and T_𝔪 the localisation. The period module of the family at 𝔪 is the T_𝔪-module P_𝔪 := M_∞(U)_𝔪 (and P⁺_𝔪 := M⁺_∞(U)_𝔪). It is faithful and finite over T_𝔪, and free over Λ′_𝒪 when U acts freely (L5/hida-freeness). It is exported as an invertible T_𝔪-module, with trivialisations P_𝔪 ≅ T_𝔪 unique up to T_𝔪^×, only under the explicit hypothesis that P_𝔪 is free of rank one over T_𝔪 (a multiplicity-one statement, proved in the minimal case by Taylor–Wiles patching in OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting); without it P_𝔪 has generic rank one at each minimal prime of T_𝔪 whose classical specialisations are newforms of level exactly U, by multiplicity one for the definite quaternion algebra and strong multiplicity one, but need not be invertible. For F = ℚ (degree one, with the indefinite modular curve in place of the definite quaternion algebra) the corresponding object is L1's family period line, and the change-of-trivialisation formula is L1/period-change-of-trivialisation.
hypotheses: F of even degree; U acting freely for the Λ′-freeness; for invertibility, the hypothesis that P_𝔪 is free of rank one over T_𝔪.
proofSteps: Faithfulness: T_∞(U, 𝒪) is defined as an algebra of endomorphisms of the tower (L5/nearly-ordinary-hecke-algebra), and localisation preserves faithfulness.

Generic rank one: at a minimal prime the dense weight-two specialisations (L5/algebraic-primes-dense) are quaternionic eigenforms whose eigenspaces in eH⁰(X(U_a), K) are one-dimensional when the corresponding Hilbert newform has level exactly U (Jacquet–Langlands and multiplicity one for D^×, HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.3).
Invertibility: a finite faithful module that is free of rank one is invertible; trivialisations differ by units. No such statement is made without the hypothesis.
acceptance: The stage's condition is visible: invertibility is a hypothesis carried by the consumer (or proved by OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting), never asserted from Λ′-freeness alone.

gaps.title: Formal-model finiteness beyond the existing geometric outline
gaps.detail: Conrad A.1.2 was read through its proof (again by R1-review). It requires Bosch–Lütkebohmert, Formal and rigid geometry I (Math. Ann. 295, 1993), Proposition 4.7 and §3.5 (rig-points, via Conrad's Lemma A.1.5), and II (Math. Ann. 296, 1993), Theorem 5.2 and Corollary 5.3 (flat and quasi-finite formal models); those primary proofs remain unread. Its scheme step is Lemma A.1.4, proved by fpqc base change to a henselian local ring, the structure theorem for separated locally quasi-finite maps (EGA IV_4 18.5.11(c)), constancy of rank over the closed fibre and spreading out of finite presentation; this was read but its EGA chain remains unexpanded. Remark A.1.3 notes that the discretely valued case is Abbes–Mokrane Lemme A.1 and that local rings of formal models are not Noetherian for nondiscrete K. R1-review supplier assessment (Task 4): no stage in data/atlas.json explicitly supplies these results in the needed generality. AdicSpacesPartII:R2 constructs admissible formal schemes, admissible blow-ups and the generic-fibre functor but states no flattening, quasi-finite-model or finiteness criterion; AdicSpacesPartII:F0 restricts formal geometry to complete Noetherian adic rings (excluding O_K for nondiscrete K) and only promises properness/separatedness/smoothness comparisons with formal models; AdicEtaleGeometry:A2 supplies admissible formal models 'in the scope required by H1' (étale cohomology); ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1 treats nondiscrete valuation bases only for nearby cycles and H1:henselian constructs affinoid henselizations, not the scheme lemma A.1.4; SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1 owns fpqc descent on the scheme side. Closest candidates, in order: AdicSpacesPartII:R2, AdicSpacesPartII:F0, AdicEtaleGeometry:A2, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1. No edge asserting supply was added; the existing R2 edge is annotated as partial.

sourceIssues.locator: §3.2, Proposition 3.3 and its proof, pp. 35–36 (Numdam PDF pages 32–33)
sourceIssues.printed: Proposition 3.3 assumes that each element of U/U∩F^× acts without fixed points on D^×\G^D(A^f). It claims that M_∞(U) and M⁺_∞(U) are free over Λ′_𝒪, with rank rank_𝒪 eH⁰(X(U⁰_1), 𝒪) times the order of the torsion subgroup of G(U). The proof says it suffices to establish this before applying e.
sourceIssues.correction: The argument shows that the Pontryagin dual of eH⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪) is projective over 𝒪[G(U_a)] and that M_∞(U), M⁺_∞(U) are projective over 𝒪[[G(U)]], hence free over Λ′_𝒪, of rank rank_𝒪(M_∞(U) ⊗_{Λ′_𝒪} 𝒪). The stated rank, and freeness over 𝒪[G(U_a)], need in addition that the ordinary parts have equal 𝒪-rank on the factors of 𝒪[G(U_a)] belonging to the different characters of the prime-to-p torsion of G(U_a).
sourceIssues.reason: e is an 𝒪[G(U_a)]-linear idempotent on the free 𝒪[G(U_a)]-module dual to H⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪), so the dual of the e-part is a direct summand, i.e. projective. 𝒪[G(U_a)] is a product of local rings indexed by the (Galois orbits of) characters of the prime-to-p part of G(U_a), and a projective module is free of the stated rank only if its ranks on these factors agree; the proof's coinvariant computation sees only the trivial character. The components correspond to nearly ordinary forms with different tame characters at p, whose dimensions the argument does not compare. Corollary 3.4 and Lemmas 3.10 and 3.19 use only freeness over Λ′_𝒪, which the argument does give.

sourceIssues.printed: Section 2 assumes the coefficient ring complete, local and noetherian with finite residue field, but the ordinary projectors are later taken over the weight algebra ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]], which for odd p is semi-local with p − 1 factors.
sourceIssues.correction: Apply §2 factor by factor over the complete local factors of the semi-local ring, reading 'perfect' as 'bounded complex of finite projective modules' (L0a/semilocal-ordinary-projector).
sourceIssues.reason: The decomposition of ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]] by the characters of μ_{p−1} makes it a product of p − 1 complete local rings; a finite projective module over the product need not be free when its ranks on the factors differ.

sourceIssues.locator: §3.2.1, the isomorphism (10) and the sentence after it, p. 25; used in the proof of Proposition 3.3(i) and (iii), p. 26 (arXiv v1)
sourceIssues.printed: Modular symbols Symb_Γ(A) are identified with a finite direct sum ⊕_i A^{Γ_i} over representatives δ_i of Δ₀/Γ whose stabilisers Γ_i are said to be finite, and it is deduced that the formation of Symb_Γ commutes with every base change in characteristic zero.
sourceIssues.correction: Δ₀ is not a permutation ℤ[Γ]-module and Δ₀/Γ is not finite; the finite description is a presentation of Δ₀ by Manin relations, exhibiting Symb_Γ(A) as the kernel of an A-linear map A^a → A^b. This gives (Pr) and compatibility with flat base change; compatibility with the specialisation R → ℚ_p at a weight needs the universal-coefficients comparison for compactly supported cohomology, with Tor terms.
sourceIssues.reason: Γ preserves the coefficients of a divisor, so the divisors n({0} − {∞}), n ≥ 1, lie in pairwise different Γ-orbits and Δ₀/Γ is infinite; moreover a modular symbol is additive, Φ(nδ) = nΦ(δ), so the values at orbit representatives are not independent and Φ ↦ (Φ(δ_i))_i is not onto a direct sum of invariants. The conclusions Bellaïche draws need the presentation of Δ₀ by Manin relations instead.
